| 586 | ANDROID-VIS.1 — Android devices appear in the staff device report | `device_tokens` held **13 iOS rows and zero Android rows ever**, despite Android staff signing in weekly. Cause: the table was keyed by `expo_push_token` (NOT NULL + UNIQUE), so a row could only exist for a device that had obtained an Expo push token — and on Android `getExpoPushTokenAsync()` throws for want of FCM credentials (never configured; the July push audit's open item). `push-register.js` swallows that failure by design, so **no row was ever written** and Android was invisible to push *and* to the geofence-permission / device-health report. **Mig 565** makes `expo_push_token` nullable and adds `device_key` (+ partial unique index, + a CHECK that one identity is always present): identity is now an app-generated per-install id persisted in SecureStore (`mobile/lib/device-key.js` — **no new native dependency, so this ships over OTA**), and the push token is an optional *capability* of that row. **Dual-identity transition:** the token's unique index STAYS, and the route ADOPTS each pre-565 row into a key (`WHERE expo_push_token = $1 AND device_key IS NULL`) before upserting, then releases the token from any row holding it under a different key — so the 13 iOS rows keep their id, history and geofence data, and a routine report can't 500 on the surviving index. `expo_push_token` is spread into the upsert **only when present** (same idiom as `geofence_permission`) — a report during a transient token failure must never silence a phone that still works. Senders now filter `expo_push_token IS NOT NULL`: `sendPush` (a `to: null` would return a ticket error counted as `failed`), `notify.js`'s fallback lookup (counting a token-less row as reachable would suppress the email and the person would get **nothing**), and the update-nudge (skips only when NONE of a person's devices has a token — judging it on the newest device would stop nudging an iPhone user the moment they signed in on Android). Sign-out deregisters by `device_key` too, so a token-less row can't keep naming a leaver. **Android push itself is still off** — that half is operator-gated on FCM credentials, documented end-to-end in the new `mobile/docs/android-fcm-setup.md` (two separate credentials; `runtimeVersion` does **not** bump — same precedent as 1.3.2 and ANDROID-R8 — and bumping would freeze every install, iOS included, off the 2.3.0 lane). No backfill needed when FCM lands: the token fills into the device's existing row. **ANDROID-VIS.1b (review fixes, mig 566):** mig 565 created the `device_key` unique index PARTIAL, and `ON CONFLICT (device_key)` cannot infer a partial index (an INSERT has no WHERE clause to imply the predicate) — verified against prod as `42P10`, so **every** report from a 2.3.x+ device would have 500'd permanently, then the sign-out DELETE (still keyed on device_key) would have ERASED rows rather than refreshed them. Mig 566 recreates it full, explicitly `NULLS DISTINCT`. The suite could not have caught it — the route's fake db always answered success — so `makeDb` now injects per-statement errors. Also: the RELEASE step was NULL-blind (`<>` is not-true for NULL), leaving a permanent-500 interleaving when a device reported token-less before its pre-565 row was adopted; a unique-violation from ADOPT now PRUNES the superseded row, and RELEASE is scoped to **non-NULL** keys because nulling the token on a key-less row would leave no identity and trip mig 565's CHECK. Identity failures no longer log-and-proceed into a doomed upsert. The health page called a token-less device 🟢 Healthy beside a live test-push button — the verdict moved to `pushHealthStatus()` in `@/lib/staff-devices` (pure + tested) with a fourth 🟡 "Visible, no push" state and a `canPush` flag that alone gates the button. `getDeviceKey()` memoizes its in-flight promise (two cold-start callers raced into two keys and an orphan row). Nudge counters split `skipped_no_app` from `skipped_no_token`. |
| 585 | HOME-FAST.1 — mobile Home cold-start: last-known-first GPS, persisted caches, optimistic tiles | Reopening the app at the studio sat on a bare spinner while auth → the geofence-config fetch → an indoor GPS acquisition serialised. Three fixes, no server change, no migration. **(1) Position reads are tiered by freshness** (`readPosition` in `use-physical-location.js`): the 45s in-process cache → the OS's last-known fix *and* our own persisted one, fresher-of-the-two (`pickFresherLastKnown`) → only then `getCurrentPositionAsync`. Acquisition used to be FIRST with last-known as a failure fallback, which is exactly backwards indoors; nothing is loosened, because `pickPosition`'s 5-minute staleness gate still bounds every tier and this is the same data the old fallback already trusted. The two explicit "I may have MOVED" signals — pull-to-refresh and a foreground after time away — pass `forceFresh`, which REORDERS the tiers (radio first) rather than deleting them: since a last-known fix would otherwise satisfy them, dropping the position cache alone had stopped forcing anything — but a failed acquisition still falls back to last-known, because an 8s indoor timeout is routine and returning "unknown" there would flip Home to its offsite layout for a phone standing in the studio, which is worse than what it replaced. **(2) Regions, the last accepted fix and the last at_studio verdict persist across launches** in SecureStore (`physical-cache.js`, studio-device.js's idiom; validation is pure + tested in `physical-snapshot.js`), hydrated once per module load. `fetchRegions` became stale-while-revalidate (TTL-fresh → return; stale but ≤24h → return immediately and revalidate in the background behind an in-flight flag; older → await), so a warm relaunch resolves with no network wait. Freshness: regions 24h, position ungated here (`pickPosition` owns it), verdict 30 min. The snapshot's `at` carries the regions' own provenance (paired atomically with the list it belongs to), so an offline relaunch re-persisting them does not re-date them. The stored verdict is a three-way decision: at_studio writes, a **confirmed offsite** clears, and `unknown` leaves it alone — "could not tell" (offline, permission denied, GPS timeout) is not evidence the phone has moved, and clearing there would cost the next launch its head start for nothing. Snapshot writes are guarded by a session generation AND a resolve sequence, so an in-flight resolve cannot re-create the file a sign-out just deleted, nor can a slow focus resolve overwrite a newer refresh's answer (state was visit-guarded; disk was not). **(3) Home paints optimistically while detecting** — `usePhysicalLocation` exposes `lastVerdict`, and under `physStatus === 'loading'` (only) Home renders that studio's `safeHomeTiles` under a GREY `detecting` pill plus an inline spinner. It never claims `detected`; a mid-detection tap is safe by construction (each destination re-resolves and wears its own pill, and the server rejects a cross-location id); an offsite answer replaces the tiles, which is correct. Home's shift list also persists (slimmed, keyed AND re-checked by profile id, index-written-first so a mid-write kill cannot orphan a value past sign-out) and paints instantly on the offsite view; it is trimmed soonest-day-first to a 1800-byte budget, because a slimmed week is ~2100 bytes and SecureStore drops an oversize value **silently** — the busiest coaches are exactly who the head start is for, and they were the only ones getting nothing. Sign-out's teardown now awaits `clearPhysicalLocationCaches()`, which also deletes both SecureStore keys — those outlive the process, so on a shared studio device they would otherwise hand the next user the previous one's regions, fix and roster. |
| 584 | SONOSGRP.1-4 — Sonos live controls per speaker group, schedule optional | Hatch connected its Sonos household but has no schedules and no favourites, and both surfaces hung the live strip off a schedule row — so a connected studio had NO live surface at all. `GET /api/sonos/now-playing` and `POST /api/sonos/control` now accept exactly one of `schedule_id` XOR `group_id` (neither/both → 400): the schedule path is behaviour-identical (its one visible delta: a mid-dispatch regroup now reads "refresh and try again"), and the group path reads **no DB row** — the active location's own token scopes the household (`withFreshToken`), so another location's group id is simply absent from the fresh groups fetch. Group ids are opaque and **ephemeral by design**, so a stale one answers the honest `regrouped` outcome (now-playing: `live:false, reason:'regrouped'`; control: 409 `code:'regrouped'`) rather than `no_group`, whose copy talks about a schedule's speakers. Web (`/automations/sonos`): a **Live now** section whenever the household answers with groups — one `SonosLiveControl` per group (name → first player's name → raw id fallback, speaker count), with a once-per-stale-episode `onRegrouped` (ref-debounced, re-armed by the next live poll) refetching the household so the section heals to the new grouping. Mobile (`/sonos`): **Live now** cards above the schedule cards via the same dual-target `SonosControlCard` + wire layer (`{ scheduleId }` or `{ groupId }`), `onStale` re-running the screen's load() under the existing focus/blur guard; with zero schedules the old "No studio music is set up…" card shrinks to a footnote below the live cards. Favourites chips already hide themselves when the list is empty, so Hatch's empty favourites cost nothing. **Publishes an OTA at 100% on merge** (`mobile/**` bundle paths); no native change, no migration. Spec `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-24-sonos-live-groups-design.md`. |

| 578 | OTAGATE.1 — the foreground OTA gate keys on background-EVIDENCE, not the previous state's name | The `prev === 'background'` gate in `foreground-update-logic.js` was correct on RN 0.86 only by grace of an upstream mapping: `RCTAppState.mm` hardcodes willEnterForeground→"background" (verified in node_modules), so real foregrounds report background→active directly — but older RNs read the live applicationState there and emitted background→INACTIVE→active, under which the gate is silently dead and phones sit on stale bundles (the exact failure this component exists to fix). The gate now tracks "did we pass through 'background' since the last real foreground" (either side of any transition counts as evidence, consumed on fire), which is behaviour-identical on 0.86 for every path — flickers (active→inactive→active) still never check or reload — and immune to the mapping changing back on an RN upgrade. +3 tests pin the older-RN sequence for both check and deferred-reload. Also corrects `use-physical-location.js`'s comment, which stated the old mapping as current fact (HOME-LOC review inherited the claim; this investigation refuted it). No migration. |

| 576 | SHELLY-MOB.1 — Shelly smart plugs on the staff mobile app: live state + on/off | Studio hub → **Smart plugs** (`mobile/app/(staff)/shelly/`): one row per adopted relay with its freshness chip, relay state and wattage, and an On/Off pill, riding `GET /api/shelly/devices` and `POST /api/shelly/devices/[id]/toggle` through `api()` (so the Bearer token, `x-active-location` **and** `x-impersonate-target` all travel — a hand-rolled header is how "View as user" silently runs as the real master). No new server code, no new permission key, no migration: it gates on the same top-level `device_control` key its routes enforce, so `shared/mobile-nav.js` needed nothing (its Studio entry has listed `device_control` since SONOSMOB.2) and `check:mobile-parity` needed only its note updated. **Authoring stays web-only on purpose** — schedules, adopt/remove, the connection and the kWh history all want a screen — and the screen says so in one line. `mobile/lib/shelly.js` is a deliberately RN-free re-typing (mobile cannot import `src/lib`) of four judgements the web already made, each pinned by `shelly.test.js` (36 tests): `output === null` is **Unknown, never Off**; the freshness windows are the engine's WRITE floor plus one missed sweep (`STATE_REFRESH_MS` + 60s / 15 min — three numbers that are one fact and must move together with `src/lib/shelly/device-health.js`); `connected === false` beats every staleness reading (after a Disconnect the rows stay adopted, so red would blame a connection someone removed on purpose) while `connected === null` never reaches red (that state is OUR read failing, not the studio's hardware); and the toggle's queued vocabulary. **The pending branch is read before anything that looks like the new state** — a saved-but-unapplied override must not paint the plug as switched — and only `connected === false` disables the buttons, because an OFFLINE plug is still settable (the route writes the override before it sends, and the cron applies it when the plug wakes). A failed 30 s poll keeps the last good rows under a subordinate retry line rather than blanking a live studio's plug list. **One additive fix in `mobile/lib/api.js`:** the toggle answers its rate-limited pending body with HTTP **429** (`success:true, pending:true`) so the client backs off instead of re-pressing, and api()'s "non-2xx without our envelope" branch replaced that body wholesale — mobile would have rendered "HTTP 429" and told an operator their switch failed when it was saved and would apply within the minute. `status` now rides that envelope (as it already did on the non-JSON branch), and `isQueued` recovers the case **by field, never by matching the error string** (the regex coupling GEOFENCE-TRANSPORT.1 removed). `geofence.js` is the only other reader of that field and gates on `transport === true`, which this branch never sets. **Publishes an OTA at 100% on merge** — trigger path `mobile/app/**`. |
| 575 | SHELLY-NAMES.3 — names from the ACCOUNT layer: `/interface/device/list` feeds the resolver when the device payload has none | SHELLY-NAMES.2 shipped and the live gate still answered *No names found for 6 plugs*, so the keys-only diagnostic was pointed at the whole v2 `get` body: it carries NO app label anywhere — `settings.sys.device.name` present-but-null and `settings.DeviceInfo.name` (the device's own GetDeviceInfo mirror) null too — because the Smart Control app's labels live in Shelly's CLOUD ACCOUNT layer, which the official v2 Cloud Control API never returns, so no widening of the v2 resolver could ever have found them. Now `client.deviceList()` calls the undocumented-but-live **`POST /interface/device/list`** (form-encoded auth like `/device/all_status`, one call, same 1 req/sec queue) — the endpoint Shelly's own web UI reads — and **`normaliseDeviceListNames`** (`src/lib/shelly/status.js`) probes its UNVERIFIED shape: entries at `data.devices` as an ARRAY or an OBJECT keyed by device id (`body.devices` tolerated), id from `id`/`_dev_info.id`/the key, label from the first non-blank of `name`/`label`/`device_name`/`alias`/`title`, ids lowercased exactly as `rawItemId` keys them and a missing name SKIPPED (absence is not an empty label). **Sync-names** asks it once, after the v2 batches, only when a covered plug is still nameless and only inside the same 8 s budget; the device's own label still wins, `unresolved` now means "neither source had one", and the ONE warning carries BOTH shapes (`shape` + `listShape`, keys/typeofs/counts only — `deviceListShapeDiagnostic`, value-leak test extended). **It is an enhancement, never a gate**: `rate_limited` or any other failure on the list is logged and the v2 names are written anyway (only `auth` parks the connection and 409s, as everywhere else) — failing a working sync because the undocumented half hiccupped would turn a partial rename into nothing. **Adopt** does the same, one conditional call on the SAME client so the pacing holds, and every failure there is non-fatal: the device is adopted nameless with the two-shape warning rather than refused over a label. |

| 571 | SHELLY-UI.1→.9 — Shelly smart plugs operator surface: /automations/shelly, /api/shelly/*, Integrations-hub card, device_control → Marketing OR Operations (mig 564) | PR 2 of the per-location Shelly integration (spec `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-22-shelly-device-control-design.md`, plan `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-23-shelly-surface.md`; PR 1 is #1500 = row 569). **Two lifts first, both behaviour-neutral for Sonos:** `src/lib/schedule/windows.js` (HHMM, `occupiedSegments`, `findWindowOverlap`, `WindowBase`, `NOT_SAME_BOUNDARY`, `windowsOverlapIssue`) and `src/components/automations/WindowsEditor.jsx` come out of the Sonos surface verbatim, so Shelly validates and edits a window with the SAME code rather than a copy — two hand-written window shapes is how the two surfaces would eventually disagree about what an empty window is, and an `on === off` window is read by the engine as a 24-hour always-on span. The Sonos route composes its `Window`/`SchedulePayload` from the shared base with the refine AFTER the extend — not because a refined schema cannot be extended (on zod 4.4.3 it is still a plain ZodObject and the refine survives `.extend`, measured and recorded in `schemas.js`) but because refining last is what keeps the same-boundary message attached to the FINAL shape rather than to the base every caller then widens — and `SonosScheduleClient` consumes the shared editor. The editor tests pin REFERENTIAL identity, not just deep equality: React bails out of a re-render on `Object.is`, so a mutate-in-place edit would deep-equal the correct result and pass every value assertion while leaving the Sonos time field snapping back under the operator. **Tenancy as shipped.** No route accepts a `location_id` at all — every query is scoped by the session's active location — and every detail route answers 404 for a malformed id AND a foreign one, with the same body, because a 400 for "that is not a uuid" beside a 404 for "not yours" is itself an oracle. **Adopt proves the device is on the CALLER'S OWN Shelly account BEFORE it looks at who holds it**: `(device_id, channel)` is UNIQUE across the whole estate (mig 562), so the holder query is necessarily cross-tenant, and running it first would make a guessed MAC answer "already in use elsewhere" for another business's hardware and "not found" otherwise — an existence oracle built out of two error messages. The gate's 404 `not_on_account` is therefore deliberately THE SAME ANSWER for "no such device" and "another tenant's device". Discovery is that rule one layer up: the ROW crosses the tenant boundary, the RESPONSE does not — a foreign holder yields the single word `elsewhere`, and a location NAME only when the holder is in the caller's own organisation (both org ids present AND equal, so a dropped embed can never name a stranger). `publicConnectionView` is an allowlist, and the key FINGERPRINT is guarded as tightly as the key: it is a sha256 OF it, so publishing it would turn "is this the account?" into an offline check anyone holding a candidate key could run. **The command surface.** The toggle writes the override FIRST, fires `setSwitch`, then stamps `last_applied`/`last_state` on success. An override is INTENT and the cron applies a live one to every adopted device, enabled or not, so a command that fails self-heals and the route answers 200 with `applied:false, pending:true` rather than an error — the one exception being a rate limit, which is HTTP 429 while the body STILL says `success:true`, because the 429 exists to stop the client re-pressing, not to say the request failed. Only the OVERRIDE write fails closed; a lost STAMP still reports `applied:true`, since the relay physically moved and telling the operator otherwise is the louder failure. On an UNMANAGED device (`enabled:false` or `schedule_mode:"none"`) the planner never closes an expired override, so the relay holds as set: those bodies carry `holds_until_changed:true` plus a notice, and the card drops the duration presets rather than rendering a countdown the engine never intended to keep. `auto` clears the override then runs the schedule now, keeping TWO answers apart (`disabled`, `no_schedule`); run-now keeps the same two apart and checks **`no_schedule` before `disabled`**, because "turn the schedule on" is useless advice when there is no schedule to turn on — and both refusals land before anything reaches the cloud, so an unmanaged device never spends a slot of the shared 1 req/s account budget to be told so. Refresh is the cron's own read step (`refreshLocationState`) behind an 8 s budget, and it judges the UN-CONFLATED engine signals `anyOk`/`budgetHit`, never the counters: `rateLimited` counts a retried SUCCESS too, and `stateWrites === 0` is the healthy answer for a studio whose readings have not moved. **Page rules the routes now depend on.** A failed 30 s poll NEVER clears rendered state — `GET /api/shelly/connection` answers 500 rather than `connection:null` precisely so a live studio is never handed the Connect form and invited to re-paste a working credential, and a client that blanked on that 500 would rebuild the failure one layer up. `GET /api/shelly/devices` carries a THIRD connection state, `connected:null` with `connection_status:"unknown"`, for "the device list read fine and the connection row did not"; only `connection_status: null` shows the Connect form. `last_state.output === null` renders as UNKNOWN, never "off". `device-health` grades `connected === false` FIRST, so a deliberate Disconnect leaves the cards reading dormant instead of a wall of red "Stale — check the Shelly connection" pointing at a connection the operator removed on purpose. An offline plug keeps its buttons live and QUEUES the toggle; only `connected === false` disables them. **Integrations hub:** one row per in-scope location, read from non-secret columns only, deep-linking to /automations/shelly. A count that could not be read stays `null` rather than becoming a confident zero, a read blip yields ONE attention row rather than one per location, and a location that is disconnected while still holding adopted plugs raises a `partialSetup` nag — which is why every in-scope location yields a row, and why `shelly` stays OUT of `HUB_STATUS_SECTIONS`. **mig 564** reseeds `private.permission_key_bundles` so `device_control` is owned by **Marketing OR Operations** (it was Marketing-only, inherited from when the key gated Sonos studio music). Widening rather than moving is what stops an Operations-only tenant being unable to switch on its own heaters. Not applied until the PR is approved for merge, never before. **Publishes an OTA at 100% on merge** — trigger path `shared/**` (`shared/permission-bundles.js` is in the Metro graph via `shared/permissions.js` → `mobile/lib/permissions.js`), and runtime 2.3.0 is the PUBLIC member lane, so the publish reaches the member fleet rather than staff phones. Content-safe for every device: a bundle-ownership widening that is behaviour-neutral at today's snapshot, and no mobile surface reads `device_control` for Shelly yet. **SHELLY-UI.9b — pre-PR review fixes.** The published contract: `ShellyErrorResponse` now carries the coded envelope for every Shelly error (the page branches on `code`, so a bare `{ success, error }` documented nothing switchable — the Sonos control route set that precedent); `connection_status` names `unknown` in its enum rather than answering an undocumented string; `SHELLY_DEVICE_ID` spells its case class instead of carrying an `i` flag, because zod-to-openapi publishes a regex as source PLUS flags and the flagged form reached the JSON-Schema `pattern` as `…$/i` — an unsatisfiable pattern every generated client would have enforced against a valid MAC; the energy 400 joins its issue `path` so it matches `validateBody`'s shape; and the operations list `BearerAuth` beside `CookieAuth`, which the toggle body's offset-form handling had already assumed. Behaviour: **device-health's green window is sized to the engine's WRITE floor, not its read cadence** — `last_seen_at` only advances when `stateChanged` fires, and a deadband-stable idle plug is rewritten only every `STATE_REFRESH_MS`, so the old 3-minute window flickered amber on every healthy plug for two minutes in five (now `STATE_REFRESH_MS + 60s` / 15 min, imported so the two numbers cannot drift apart). **`nothing_to_do` was unreachable and is gone**: `runNowForDevice` forces, and under force the planner's only null path is rule 2 (unmanaged), which both routes already answer as `disabled`/`no_schedule` — so "already correct" could only ever have been a claim about a state nobody checked; a no-op reaching either route is now a logged 500 (`unexpected_noop`). The un-managing notice fires for `schedule_mode:'none'` on an enabled device too (rule 2 has two arms, and clearing a schedule abandons the relay exactly as thoroughly as switching it off), and the schedule editor surfaces it the way the enable toggle already did. `ShellyToggleBody` is `.strict()`, so an `untill` typo is a 400 rather than a silent fall-through to midnight. The toggle's optimistic `last_state` nulls the measurements it did not take — carrying old watts under a FRESH `at` re-dates a reading taken while the relay was off and renders it as a live measurement of one we just switched on. `device_count` never defaults an uncomputed count to 0 (PostgREST answers null with no error, and the panel spends that number on "your N plugs stay adopted"). And an unmanaged override the engine ALREADY closed no longer resurrects its banner: a device that was managed when the override expired carries `last_applied.reason 'override_expired'` with that override's key, and the card checks it. **LIVE EXIT GATE — three payload shapes still unverified against the real Stillorgan account** (all three were read from Shelly's docs, not from a live key, and each has a route resting on it). (1) `/v2/devices/api/get` must return items for OWNED ids ONLY, silently omitting any id the key cannot see — that is what makes "the id came back" equal "this account owns it", and `POST /api/shelly/devices` already logs "cloud get echoed an id with no device data — ownership gate may be void" for exactly the shape that would void it. (2) The v1 `all_status` NAME location: `normaliseAllStatus` reads the entry's own name and falls back to `_dev_info.name`, so a real account that puts it somewhere else renders a wall of MACs on the first Find devices. | 569 | SHELLY.1→.12 — Shelly smart-plug backend: tz-aware engine, paced cloud client, exactly-once planner, energy roll, per-location reconcile cron (migs 562/563) | PR 1 of the per-location Shelly integration (spec `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-22-shelly-device-control-design.md`, plan `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-22-shelly-backend.md`). Dormant until an owner pastes a key in PR 2; the cron stamps `locations: 0` meanwhile — and only a COMPLETED tick stamps the heartbeat (`out.ok !== false`): a connection-load failure or an unusable clock deliberately does not, so the 900 s grace absorbs one blip while a sustained one pages. **Tenancy:** one Shelly account per location (`shelly_connections.location_id UNIQUE`); the key fingerprint is deliberately NOT unique (an owner with two studios may run both on one account — same-org sharing is allowed, cross-org refused in app code, and a blank org id can never match); `shelly_devices (device_id, channel)` is UNIQUE **globally** so a relay channel can never serve two locations. **Command model** = boundary exactly-once (the Sonos `planAction` shape) with STRING keys, plus a two-way override applied once for every adopted device, enabled or not; a failed command is never stamped so a late on/off self-heals; a class-occurrence LOAD ERROR skips class devices rather than reading as "no classes" (and a stale expired override cannot defeat that skip — `isLiveOverride`). **Rate limit** is 1 req/s per ACCOUNT, so connections are grouped by key fingerprint — accounts in parallel, same-account studios serial — with `MAX_GET_IDS`-batched reads, ≤1 `set/groups` per direction, calls serialised inside the client, one 429 retry, and a 1 s handoff between two locations of one account (each builds its own client, and a fresh one believes it has never called). Connections are swept oldest-`last_ok_at` first (nulls first) so a short budget rotates round the estate; a failing one is PARKED rather than hammered — `action_needed` 15 min, `error` 5 min (`ERROR_RETRY_MS`) — and the first failed read batch *before any success* ends that tick's reads AND skips its commands (the black-hole stop). `connected` requires at least one 2xx **and** no hard 429 that tick (`budgetHit`), so a studio whose relays did not move never shows green; a `get` answering 2xx with a top-level `error` body is a FAILED read, not an empty one — read as success it is exactly "the account answered and mentioned nobody", which writes every device offline under a connected badge. **`src/lib/tz-time.js` is new** (dublin-time.js is pinned by the shared-pair test) and it fixes a latent engine bug found on the way: the old minute-of-day guess-and-correct was a whole day late for Dublin 23:00–23:59 boundaries during IST (no live Sonos window has one — latest is 20:31) and a day out for every negative-offset zone; a skipped local midnight now resolves to the first instant of the day. **Absent is not zero**, everywhere: `Number(null) === 0` would have minted 0 W readings, fake energy resets and a silent-epoch day key — typed coercion in status, energy and tz-time. **Energy**: `wh_total` is a sum of positive deltas with reset (<½) vs rollback handling, 3-dp rounding that telescopes (no drift), a 7-day carry window (`ENERGY_LOOKBACK_DAYS`); read per device with an explicit column projection (never `*`: the row round-trips into the upsert) and `ENERGY_ROW_CAP` pinning the worst case — a location-wide 30-day read breaks the 1k cap. **Two diagnostics gated on CHANGE** (the v2 id echo, the v2 `online` field): a never-read device counts as a transition, so day one still names the bug while a genuinely dark studio stays quiet. **Secrets**: the key rides in the query string / v1 form body, so the client never logs a URL or body, `redactSecret` strips raw, URL-encoded and form-encoded forms, and the host is re-validated inside the client (SSRF) as well as by a DB CHECK. 563 (heartbeat) applied only AFTER the deploy, and it also carries the forward correction of 562's `status` column comment — 562 is already applied, so a comment it got wrong is corrected forward, never edited in place. |

(4) **Staff create** — a failed `profiles` update creates the staff member with the DEFAULT role/permissions/comp and still answers 201; the sibling `profile_locations` delete leaves the trigger's default grant underneath the requested ones. (5) **Mobile member auto-link** discarded the contacts read error and handed `shouldAttemptLinkContact` a hard-coded `NO_MEMBER`, so a transient failure read as CONFIRMED-empty and fired the silent self-link; now routed through `probeMember()`, guarded by a source-scanning test since `mobile/**` is outside `check:guardrails`. (6) **Event sender resolution** discarded both read errors and the tier logic falls through on a null. (7) **`whatsapp-consent.js`**, found in the residue sweep and worse than any of the sites this set out to fix: both paths wrote the three consent rows as bare awaits inside a try/catch that CANNOT fire for a supabase result, so a failed STOP answered `applied: true` and texted the customer "You've been unsubscribed" while they stayed in every marketing audience. (8) The **WhatsApp drip** claimed its recipient row AFTER the send with a bare upsert, so a lost row re-sent the same marketing template next tick. (9) The **Instagram send `warnings`** array nothing had ever read — `IGInbox.handleSend` now renders it. **THE HARDER HALF, and what four review rounds were actually spent on: removing a silent failure must never create a LOUDER one.** Four fail-closed "fixes" shipped on this branch and all four were reversed before merge. (a) The consent fix returned early on the first failed write, so a partial failure left ZERO suppression signals where `main` left one. Both paths now share one `applyConsentWrites` helper that ATTEMPTS every write regardless, collects failures, then judges: STOP is `applied` when EITHER gate landed (audience flag or `wa_status` — either alone keeps the contact out of real traffic), START only when BOTH did (a partial opt-in leaves them suppressed, so the acknowledgement would be a promise not kept). Partials return `partial: true` + `failures[]` through `logError('wa-consent', …)`. (The helper is insurance, not a repair — the two paths had NOT previously drifted; 85afb1c0 moved both to `.upsert` in one commit.) (b) `resolveEventCommsLocation` threw on an unreadable `locations` row; `sendRaceConfirmations` caught it and returned before sending, every caller answers 200, and `markRacePaymentStatus` returns `applied: null` once a payment is already `completed` — so one blip = one paying attendee with no receipt and no check-in QR, permanently. `payment-sms` answered 503 on an operator's explicit action, and the reminders cron `continue`d on a comment claiming "the next tick re-attempts" when that cron is DAILY against a fixed day-offset, so a skipped tick DESTROYED the reminder. **The resolver now never throws**; every discarded read degrades to `null` with a structured `logError` carrying `crossesLocation`. What the throw bought: email identity resolves per ORGANISATION (structural), and — measured read-only against prod 2026-08-20 across all 13 `race_events` — no event resolves to a (target, fallback) pair whose Twilio alpha senders differ. **That second half is a fact about the data, not the code: Hatch Street (`UN1THATCH`) and Stillorgan (`UN1T Dub`) are in the same org and DO differ**, and the guarantee holds only because the single Hatch event is plain (no host, no `sending_location_id`). The SQL that reproduces it, and the condition that ends it, are in the source. (c) **Claim-before-send.** Race stamps went back to send-then-stamp with the error read and `logError`'d, keeping the `.is(col, null)` CAS so a concurrent stamp is reported as `duplicate_send` — a duplicate receipt is an annoyance, a missing one means the attendee cannot check in. The **drip** keeps claim-first, because that row has a status lattice a lease can hang on, but the claim is now a LEASE: `created_at` is the claim stamp, `claimDripRecipient` re-claims a `'pending'` row older than `STUCK_CLAIM_MINUTES` (60), and `fetchDripDoneContactIds` re-opens it. Without that, a process kill between claim and send dropped that contact's drip step forever and invisibly — the earlier defence that "a stuck `'pending'` is visible" was false: `unaccounted` is rendered only when the broadcast also has capped rows, and reads "have not been attempted yet". `claimDripRecipient` is also a real mutex now: the blast INSERTs (mig 331's UNIQUE rejects a concurrent pass) while the drip UPSERTed, which succeeds on conflict, so two overlapping ticks both sent; INSERT for a fresh contact, `UPDATE … WHERE status='capped'` for the Meta-131049 retry the upsert existed for, `UPDATE … WHERE status='pending' AND created_at < cutoff` for an abandoned claim. (d) **A lost bookkeeping write is never grounds to KILL the work.** `campaignFailurePatch` flips a campaign to `failed` once `last_error` is already set, `send_started_at` is null and it is past the grace window — and the bundle gate writes `last_error` EVERY tick by design, while the cron never clears `last_error` at all. So a returned `error` from a rotation bump killed a campaign on its first blip, and the same from the empty-audience finalise (which runs inside populate, `send_started_at` still null) killed any campaign carrying an older error. Both are `result.warning` now: logged at error level and counted in `summary.warnings`, never fed to the kill switch, and the campaign keeps `main`'s self-healing loop. **Tests.** `tests/guardrails-rules.test.js` reproduces the write-side defect shapes verbatim as `invalid` cases, so the suite demonstrates the rule would have caught them at PR time. Every behavioural change has a test that was run against the previous branch code and observed to FAIL — including `race-confirmations.commslocation.test.js`, which deliberately does NOT mock the resolver, because mocking it at the seam is what let the two halves drift (the resolver's suite proved it threw, race-confirmations' proved the throw was caught, and nobody asked what the customer received). No migrations. Prod was read READ-ONLY, for the sender measurement. PR #1472. |

The whole *"An existing contact could not be found"* failure was therefore never a stale cache — it was purely the wrong-org binding, exactly as reported. The `pullContacts`-on-org-change behaviour from #1471 remains correct as a safety net; only the claim that Stillorgan needed it was wrong. |

| 550 | XERO-ONE-ORG.3 — the rule is now structural: `UNIQUE(tenant_id)` (mig 554) | Applied the moment the data allowed it. The database itself now refuses a second location on the same Xero org, which is what makes the rule survive a future code path that forgets to ask — an importer, a script, a hand-written INSERT. **Verified against the live table, not assumed**: an INSERT binding a second location to Champ Fitness's tenant is rejected with `duplicate key value violates unique constraint "xero_connections_tenant_id_unique"`, and `get_advisors` after the DDL returns only the pre-existing estate-wide INFO lints — nothing new. The redundant non-unique `xero_connections_tenant_idx` is dropped (the constraint brings its own index). **Second defect found while checking the state:** disconnecting a location deleted its `xero_connections` row but left its caches behind — they key on `location_id`, which survives a disconnect, so nothing cascaded. CCF Autos' disconnect had stranded **509 rows** (415 contacts, 78 accounts, 16 tax rates) belonging to an org it is no longer connected to; reconnect that location to a DIFFERENT org and the pickers would have offered the old company's contacts and account codes, which is the exact wrong-org failure this series exists to stop. The disconnect route now purges all three (after deleting the connection, so a partial failure leaves stale cache on a disconnected location rather than a live connection with none), and the migration clears what earlier disconnects left. |

| 548 | XERO-ONE-ORG.1 — one location, one Xero organisation, enforced in code | **Operator-reported, and a real accounting exposure.** All three connected locations (UN1T Stillorgan, CCF Autos, SourceIt) were bound to the SAME Xero tenant — `b8a764df…` "Givers Consultancy LTD" — so three separate legal entities were filing bills into one company's books. **101 bills, ~€99,300** had already gone in that way (Stillorgan 84 / ~€90,568; SourceIt 17 / €8,781.05; CCF Autos 0). **Cause: one line.** `callback/route.js` did `const tenant = tenants[0]`, on the written assumption that "most users have a single tenant anyway". Xero's `/connections` returns EVERY org the login has ever authorised (the consent screen accumulates grants), so "the first one" was the same org on all three connects — 19 May, 24 May and 6 Jul, each a separate OAuth run by the same operator, who was never shown a choice. Nothing checked whether the org was already spoken for. The intent had always been the opposite: migration 029's comment says the tenant is chosen "**explicitly** so we know which org to push into", and `INTEGRATIONS.md` repeats it — the callback simply never implemented it. **Fixed:** new pure `tenant-binding.js` (`classifyTenants` / `chooseTenantToBind` / `validateTenantChoice`, 14 tests written against the real three-location failure) — the callback now **never binds an org another location holds**, refuses outright when every granted org is taken (naming which location holds each), and when several are free it says which one it took so a wrong auto-pick is visible immediately instead of months later. New `GET/POST /api/xero/select-tenant` + a "Change organisation" control on the settings card let an operator repoint a location **without re-running OAuth** — the stored refresh token already grants every org in the list, which is what makes remediation possible at all; previously the only way to correct a binding was to re-auth and hope the right org came back first, i.e. the same dice roll that caused this. Switching **purges the per-location `xero_accounts` / `xero_contacts` / `xero_tax_rates` caches and their sync stamps** and re-primes from the new org, because every id in them is org-specific — leaving them would let an operator pick an account code that does not exist in the new org and get an opaque Xero validation error at send time. **Deliberately NOT done:** (a) already-pushed bills are not moved — that is an accounting decision (void and re-enter, or a journal), not a settings toggle; (b) the `UNIQUE(tenant_id)` index that would make the rule structural is **not** in this PR, because it would fail against current prod data where three rows share a tenant — apply it once each location is on its own org. **Correction to an earlier claim in this session:** it was asserted that every cached account/contact came from the shared org. That was wrong, and measured to be wrong — SourceIt's 354 cached contacts share **zero** ids with Stillorgan's 461, while Stillorgan ∩ CCF Autos is 415 of 415, so at least two orgs' data is present and the caches predate the current bindings. 14 tests. Full suite 15,638 green. |
| 547 | POSTMARK-RACE.2 — the deferral #546 introduced was correct and then cost three things nobody had priced | Review of #546 against prod found the same mistake three times: **a deferral was sized against the race window and never against what a deferral now costs.** **(1) Recovery inherited a queue.** Answering QStash 200 retires the message, and #546 handed every deferral to the `*/10` sweeper on the strength of "10 minutes is ~45x the worst commit lag (13.2s)". That sizes the WAIT, not the THROUGHPUT: `BATCH_SIZE = 100` on a `*/10` schedule is a hard ceiling of 600 rows/hour, and a campaign burst produces **~1,000 raced events in a single 10-minute window** (peak measured 1,038). Prod on **2026-08-10** shows the ceiling, not the backlog, setting the rate — 543 + 488 rows cleared instantly by QStash at 18:02/18:04, then **exactly 100 per tick at 18:10, 18:20, 18:31, 18:40, 18:50, 19:00 and on past 21:40**; max queue lag over 60 days is 4h15m and 46% of rows already take >60s. The 1,031 rows QStash used to clear instantly are precisely the population that now defers, so they would have been appended to a queue already hours behind — with one-click unsubscribes and hard bounces sharing the same FIFO. Fixed with a remedy already in the codebase and unused: `publishQueuePush({ delaySeconds })` sets `Upstash-Delay`, so a deferred row now **re-publishes itself at +60s** (~4.5x the worst lag) with an **attempt-scoped** dedup id — `postmark-queue-<id>-r<attempts>`, because reusing the ingest id `postmark-queue-<id>` lands inside QStash's dedup window and is silently swallowed, the same trap the host-campaign self-chain hit. The implementer's objection stands intact: QStash's OWN fast retries still must not do the retrying, since they fire inside the window they cannot outrun. `BATCH_SIZE` 100 → **300** with an explicit `maxDuration = 300` and a `TIME_BUDGET_MS` guard so the sweeper is a real guarantee for a QStash outage rather than a formality. **(2) The marker said "a row WAS written"; the processor read it as "a row IS coming".** `email_sends_contact_id_fkey` is **`ON DELETE CASCADE`** (verified on prod via `pg_constraint`) and deleting a contact is the estate's routine GDPR-erasure action (`/api/contacts/bulk-delete`, `/api/contacts/[id]`, import rollback), while Open/Click webhooks arrive **p50 1.9h, p95 6.8 days, max 44.4 days** after the send (n=5,189/60d). So "marked send → contact erased → a late Open lands" is reachable, and a constant marker could not tell it from a 13-second race: five retries over ~40 minutes and then a `webhook_dead_letter` row under the deliberately **non-replayable** `postmark_queue` provider (it stays `pending` until a human deals with it) carrying `send_row_not_yet_committed` — a false statement about an event that is correctly unrecordable. Latent, not active: zero `campaign-<uuid>` events in the 21-day no-row population, so no erasure has collided with a campaign yet. `crm_send` now carries **`String(Date.now())`** (13 of the 80 available chars) and the processor defers only inside a **5-minute** window; older-and-missing is provably not racing, so it drops with a warn naming the marker's age — the honest outcome for an erased contact and a *diagnosable* one for the other case. Unreadable or implausible marker → still defers, so the rule can only get stricter than #546, never looser (this is also what protects an in-flight `crm_send: '1'` across the deploy). The related silent hole is closed at source: `sendTransactionalEmail`/`sendMarketingEmail` **discarded their `email_sends` insert error**, so a genuinely failed insert — the case that SHOULD be an incident — produced no artefact at all; both now log it. **(3) The deferred retry made a non-idempotent write reachable.** `.update({ status: 'delivered', delivered_at })` was guarded on `delivered_at` alone, which was safe only because a raced Delivery used to be processed exactly once, immediately. Post-#546 it comes back minutes later, by which time an `Open` may legitimately have advanced `email_sends.status` — and the row is downgraded `opened` → `delivered`, the exact regression #546's own backfill SQL was written to prevent (`CASE WHEN es.status = 'sent'`). Measured: **1,205 of the 3,231 recoverable prod rows are already `opened`/`clicked`**, 114 of them opened within 10 minutes of the send. Adding `.eq('status','sent')` to the single UPDATE would have been **worse** — it would match zero rows for an opened send, `deliveredSends` would come back empty, the count probe would find the row and `delivered_at` would be lost again, reintroducing the whole defect. So the write is **split**, mirroring the backfill: `delivered_at` unconditionally under the unchanged `.is('delivered_at', null)` transition guard (still exactly-once, still the thing the counter rides), then `status` promoted separately under `.eq('status','sent')`. Blast radius was checked rather than assumed — `recalculate_campaign_stats` counts from the timestamps, `bounce-escalation` falls back to them, and nothing filters `email_sends.status = 'opened'` — so the damage was per-send hygiene (contact drawer, `contact-export`), not stats. Sibling `campaign_recipients` write was already correctly guarded. Backfill still NOT applied — SQL in the PR body, now written to promote status only from `sent`. |
| 546 | POSTMARK-RACE.1 — a Delivery webhook that outran its `email_sends` row stopped being thrown away | The Vercel error `Delivery for unknown message … Suspect the send-loop insert race` was right about the cause and wrong about the scale. **Prod, 21 days: 3,231 of 10,191 Delivery events (32%) were processed BEFORE their `email_sends` row committed, and every one lost its delivery** — `delivered_at` NULL on 3,231/3,231 of them and set on 6,960/6,960 of the rest, a clean split with nothing else left to explain it. `postmark_message_id` is minted by Postmark, so no send path can write its row before the API returns; the campaign path sends a batch of up to 500 first, and the webhook lands 1-2s later. **Write-first is therefore impossible** — the id does not exist yet. So `src/lib/postmark-send-marker.js` adds an explicit correlation marker, `Metadata.crm_send`, stamped at exactly the five send sites that write an `email_sends` row and gated on exactly the condition each of them already gates its insert on (`contactId` / `contact?.id` / `ticket.contact_id`). Postmark echoes `Metadata` verbatim on every record type (confirmed on 16k stored payloads). Marked + no row = a race, so the handler returns not-ok and the queue row goes back to pending with attempts+1; unmarked + no row = not ours, dropped exactly as before and **no longer at `console.error`** (~31/day of ignorable noise at error level is what buried this for months). The `SubscriptionChange` REACTIVATION branch is deliberately exempt — it resolves by `Recipient` and "no send row" is its normal path. New outcome status `deferred` answers QStash **200** instead of 500: QStash retries within seconds and would spend the whole budget inside a window it cannot outrun (worst measured commit lag 13.2s, p50 8.1s, p95 11.3s, nothing beyond 60s), so recovery is handed to the 10-minute sweeper — ~45x margin. New `describeApiError()` (`src/lib/api-error.js`, 10 tests) folds the issues in, wired into all **7** of the inbox's error paths. It matches the field name on a **word boundary**, not a substring, so `total` is not suppressed by "Subtotal is required" — a naive `includes()` would have hidden exactly the field the operator needs; and it caps at three issues so a whole-object failure is not a wall of text. 20 tests added. | 543 | RECEIPT-NULLS.1 + MIME-SNIFF.1 — the two errors sitting in the invoice inbox, and the classes behind them | Both surfaced as stuck rows an operator asked about, and both are cases of the extractor being told something untrue about a file. **(1) A receipt is not an invoice.** `invoice_number` and `invoice_date` were non-nullable in `invoiceFieldsSchema`, so when Claude correctly answered `null` for a Tesco till receipt with no readable date, validation failed and the **entire extraction was discarded** — supplier, total and line items included — leaving the operator a schema error and no data (row `ee83a2f6`; an identical `invoice_number` failure had already killed card receipt `e216cb1b` in June, unnoticed). Defaulting to `received_at` was rejected — a bill's `Date` drives the **VAT period**, so an invented date misfiles the return quietly and in the direction nobody audits. `InvoiceNumber`/`Reference` are optional on an ACCPAY bill, so a numberless receipt now **omits** the keys (same conditional-spread idiom as `DueDate`) instead of posting an explicit null, and the line description no longer reads "Invoice  from Tesco Ireland". **(2) The stored mime was a lie.** `enqueueFromContractorInvoice` hard-coded `attachment_mime_type: 'application/pdf'` and a null size — because its source column is named `pdf_path` — while **every other enqueue path reads the real mime from its source row**. Contractors upload phone photos: James Barr's `.png` went to Anthropic inside a `document` block and returned `"The PDF specified was not valid"` (400), an error naming neither the file nor the real cause (row `ad57c308`; Storage had it correct as `image/png` all along, which is how the live row was repaired by hand). Fixed at **both** layers, on purpose: enqueue now resolves mime+size from Storage with an extension fallback and **never fails the enqueue over metadata** (a queue row with an imperfect mime is recoverable; a missing one is an invoice nobody gets paid for), and `extractInvoiceFieldsFromBytes` now **sniffs the actual bytes** (`sniffMimeFromBytes`) and trusts them over the label — which closes the class for every source, past and future, not just the one that was wrong. The sniffer returns null rather than guessing on an unknown signature, so an unidentifiable file yields the clear "Unsupported MIME type for OCR" message instead of a confusing vendor 400; it checks both halves of the RIFF container so a `.wav` is never called a WebP. 22 tests added (schema nulls, confidence tie-in, 8 signature cases, 4 enqueue mime cases, Xero guard + payload omission). Full suite 15,443 green. |
| 542 | TOKENDEAD.1 — the un1t tokens UI-FOUND.1 renamed away were still in 203 places, and still being written | Reported as a UI question, not a bug: an operator asked what was supposed to be inside the **black box** on `/offer-sales`. | 541 | ZOOMSYNC.4 — the Zoom contact sync stopped enqueueing numbers Zoom refuses, and parks the ones it still refuses | The nightly reconcile had been failing on the same rows since 2026-08-06: **280 runtime errors in 7 days** on `/api/webhooks/qstash/zoom-contacts`, all `400 … must be E.164 format` (`+87654567890`, `+800860588525`, `+35382247706573`, `+35386921983289`). Two independent defects. **(1) Nothing validated the number before enqueue.** `normaliseForZoom()` answers a SHAPE question (separators, bidi marks, trunk zeros, bare national numbers); everything it returns *looks* like E.164 and was published on that basis. New `src/lib/zoom/publishable-e164.js` answers the second question: assigned ITU country calling code (`87` is not one), global service codes excluded (`+800` is UIFN, not a person), no national trunk zero after the country code (`+4407502871075`, `+9109607976617`, `+35300000000` are live rows), and a national-length bound for the three markets we have authority over — **IE 7-10, GB 7-10, NANP exactly 10**, which is what rejects the two `+353` numbers hard E.164 accepts. **(2) A permanent 400 was retried like a transient 500.** The worker now classifies: 4xx (except 401/408/429) is a verdict on the payload, so the job is dead-lettered to `webhook_dead_letter` under provider `zoom_contact_sync` and answered **200** — QStash stops, the reconcile skips it (`loadParkedNumbers()` reads pending rows of that provider), and resolving the row on `/admin/webhook-dead-letter` is the un-park. Deliberately **not** in `src/lib/webhook-replay.js`'s registry, same reasoning as `postmark_queue`: a replay re-asks a settled question. **The delete trap, handled explicitly.** Removing a key from desired is not neutral — `diffContacts()` reads "in Zoom, not in desired" as a DELETE, and the guard would not catch it (threshold `max(20, 5%)` ≈ 317 against a population of ~2). So the diff takes `protectedKeys` and withholds creates, updates AND deletes for them; case (a) numbers Zoom never created are simply no-ops, case (b) numbers Zoom already holds are **left alone** rather than deleted. It self-clears: the set is recomputed from the CRM each run, so once the operator fixes the number the old key leaves the set and the stale entry deletes through the normal guarded path. **Strictness was measured, not chosen.** Against the live desired set (6,339 distinct numbers, 19 Aug, read-only prod SQL): these rules reject **12**, and the nightly permanent-failure floor is ~10-13 creates — while `libphonenumber-js` `isValid()` on full metadata rejects **69**, of which ~56 are numbers Zoom **accepted** and is holding today (odd landline lengths, wrong prefixes). Adopting it would have stripped those members off the handsets, and it is lenient about the trunk-zero splices Zoom actually rejects — so no dependency was added; only its *possible-length* metadata was read at design time. **Operator visibility, on existing surfaces only:** `/settings/integrations/zoom-contacts` gains an `invalid_e164` group in the same "Contacts the sync cannot use" report (rendered from the SAME `buildDesiredContacts()` call the sync uses, so it cannot drift), with a per-row **Problem** column naming the broken rule; the run summary and `cron_heartbeats.last_outcome` carry the withheld counts; parked rows appear on `/admin/webhook-dead-letter` with a label and a number-first summary. The run envelope carries **counts only, never a list of numbers** — the guard sample already had to be redacted for callers without `integrations_zoom_manage`, and a second list would reopen that leak. Counts ride in the existing `stats` jsonb, so **no migration**. Note the design record's "`buildDesiredContacts` reads ALL contacts with no org filter" is stale — ZOOMSYNC.2 (#466) closed it and it is verified closed here (prod: UN1T Group 8,609 contacts, CCF Autos 0, Givers 0); scope deliberately not widened further. 45 new tests (validator table-driven over the four logged numbers plus every number in the live set these rules reject, permanent-vs-transient classification, and the delete-trap cases). **Adversarial review round (same PR) found three defects, all fixed.** (1) **The trunk-zero rule's own comment claimed it "is wrong in every country". It is not.** Italy is the standing exception — since the 1998 renumbering the leading 0 *is* the landline number, so `+39 06…` (Rome) and `+39 02…` (Milan) are correct E.164 and were being rejected, as were San Marino (`+378 0549…`) and Côte d'Ivoire's 2021 10-digit plan (`+225 07…`). A latent false-reject, not a live one — prod holds 4 Italian contacts and read-only SQL confirms **0** of them are landlines (`digits LIKE '390%'` = 0) — but the harm lands on the next Italian landline entered, and over-rejection is precisely the expensive direction this file's own header names. Now `NSN_KEEPS_LEADING_ZERO` guards the check, with the exception list documented as **non-exhaustive on purpose** (Gabon +241 is the likely next member, left out as unconfirmed and zero-exposure) and self-announcing: an omitted country shows up in the rejects report under "Country code followed by a national 0". An all-zero NSN is still rejected so the exemption is not a placeholder hole. (2) **"Discard" on `/admin/webhook-dead-letter` re-armed the exact nightly loop this PR exists to kill.** `loadParkedNumbers()` filtered `status='pending'`, so Discard — which sets `discarded` — dropped the row out of the suppression set and put the number straight back in the next night's diff: re-enqueue → Zoom 400 → a NEW pending row, every night, one extra dead-letter row each time. Semantically it was backwards: Discard is the operator saying "this number is not getting fixed", i.e. the one case where suppression must PERSIST, and it was the only button that resumed the write. Filter is now `.in('status', ['pending','failed','discarded'])` — **resolve, and only resolve, un-parks** — and the Discard confirm copy is provider-aware (`discardConfirmText()`), since "it stays on record" described the opposite of what happened. (3) **No circuit breaker on parking.** `isPermanentZoomFailure()` cannot distinguish a bad phone number from Zoom refusing the whole ACCOUNT — a dropped `phone:write:external_contact` scope, a lapsed Zoom Phone plan or an external-contact quota all return 4xx on *every* write, which on a cold start is ~6,300 of them, each parking a row and permanently suppressing its number, recoverable only one click at a time. One credential fault would have been laundered into thousands of permanent suppressions. Added `PARK_BUDGET = 50` (`parkingBudgetExhausted()`): past it the worker **stops parking and returns 500** — loud, retryable, nothing suppressed — because a systemic failure should stay a transient rather than be converted into permanent state. It fails OPEN (an unreadable count never blocks the per-number parking that fixes the live loop), the opposite direction to `loadParkedNumbers()`, which fails open on suppression. Also added `.order('received_at')` to the parked read so behaviour past `PARKED_LIMIT` degrades deterministically instead of returning an arbitrary subset, and `POST /api/admin/webhook-dead-letter/bulk-resolve` (master/owner, **one named provider only** — a blanket clear would let a Zoom cleanup silently acknowledge unread inbound email) with a "Resolve all N" control that appears once a provider filter is chosen. Prod check: `webhook_dead_letter` is currently **empty**, so the first post-merge run parks from zero. Re-measured the desired set by running the REAL `normaliseForZoom` + `e164Rejection` over all **6,478** distinct prod phone strings (UN1T Group, non-ClassPass, named): 6,339 E.164 candidates, **12 rejected** (5 `national_length`, 4 `trunk_zero`, 2 `unassigned_country_code`, 1 `service_number` — all four originally-logged numbers among them), **desired = 6,327**, and the new trunk-zero exemption rescues **0** numbers today, i.e. the loosening is provably a no-op against live data and purely forward-looking. Suite 15,552 green; 280 tests across the Zoom + dead-letter surface. |
| 540 | OTA-PATHS.1 — the OTA publish trigger becomes an allowlist, not a denylist | `eas-update.yml` publishes a real OTA to production phones on every qualifying push to `main`. Its trigger was `mobile/**` with `!` negations bolted on per incident, and it failed twice in eight days: **#1451** (`ddf01aef`, 08-18) published from a docs-only push, and **#1434** (`2ce8971c`, 08-17) published from a push whose only mobile file was `mobile/.audit-allowlist.json`. #1455 answered the first with a single negation (`!mobile/docs/**`) — the symptom, not the class; the second was still open, along with `asc-screenshots/`, `certs/`, `scripts/`, `eas.json`, `.eas/`, `.env.example`. Verified against the Actions API, not inferred: the run list shows `2ce8971c` succeeded (which also settles empirically that `mobile/**` matches **dotfiles**) and shows no run for `e8d68ff1` (so #1455's negation did work, and is preserved). Urgency: `store-release-one-app.md` §4 has the operator commit fresh App Store screenshots during the launch, which under `mobile/**` would mint a new update group at 10% **on top of the already-100%-ramped 2.3.0 lane** — devices outside the new cohort fall back to the older group, plus a 48h ramp-or-rollback obligation for a no-op. **Decision: allowlist.** Both failure modes are bad — a denylist miss publishes something unwanted (loud but expensive to undo: republish the last good group), an allowlist miss publishes nothing (silent but cheap to undo: one `workflow_dispatch` click). The tiebreak is that the allowlist's silence is *fixable* and the denylist's is not: `check:ota-paths` fails the moment a new top-level entry under `mobile/` is neither in the trigger nor in a `NON_BUNDLE` map, so the miss surfaces on the PR that creates the directory. A denylist admits no equivalent guard — detecting "a new non-bundle path appeared" needs the same classification list, and once you have it the allowlist is strictly safer because an **unclassified path defaults to "don't publish"**. 12 of 21 top-level `mobile/` entries publish; 9 are inert. `mobile/assets/**` is IN despite looking like store art — the Archivo fonts are `require()`d from `app/_layout.jsx:177`, so Metro ships them. `shared/**` stays **wholesale on purpose**: mobile imports 48 of 119 modules by direct static grep, which misses shared→shared transitive pulls and churns weekly, so a missed OTA for a real shared change beats an extra publish for a web-only one. The guard also rejects `!` negations (denylist creep), dead patterns after a rename, and narrowing `shared/**`; `tests/ota-trigger-paths.test.js` (41 tests) is the fires/does-not-fire table, calibrated against the three real runs above. web-ci now watches `.github/workflows/eas-update.yml` — without it, editing the trigger skipped the only check that reads it. Sibling workflows deliberately left broad: `mobile-export.yml` and `web-ci.yml` trigger on `mobile/**` but **publish nothing** (`expo export` to a temp dir / tests), so for them an extra run is free and a missed run is a coverage hole — the asymmetry is inverted. Runbooks reconciled (`ota-rollout.md`, `store-release-one-app.md`, `architecture/MOBILE.md`), since an operator following a stale runbook is how this class keeps recurring. **Adversarial review round (same PR) found a blocker the allowlist did not close:** `npm run version:patch` is documented step 1 of BOTH per-version store-submission flows, and it edited `mobile/app.config.js` → committed → tagged → **pushed, by default** — and `app.config.js` is pattern #7 of the new allowlist. Because `version` (`app.config.js:110`) and `runtimeVersion` (`:375`) are **separate literals**, the resulting group lands on the *currently live* runtime lane, demoting the ~90% already on the ramped group and starting a fresh 48h clock. With build 24 in Apple review and the 2.3.0 lane at 100%, an operator following the runbook would have fired an unplanned production OTA. Fixed: `bump-version.mjs` push is now **opt-in** (`--push`) and **refuses `main` outright**; the consequence is printed; `MOBILE.md` steps 1 (iOS + Android), `.eas/workflows/release.yml`'s pre-flight and a new **launch-window freeze** callout in `store-release-one-app.md` §8 all say so. Review also corrected three overclaims written into the artifact itself: "recovery is one click" → one `workflow_dispatch` **plus a manual ramp** (it takes no inputs, so it publishes from **main HEAD** at the same hard-coded 10%); "`check:ota-paths` fails CI / forces the choice" → on PRs it is a **signal, not a gate** (`main` has no branch protection and no rulesets — verified via the API), so the check was **added to `eas-update.yml`'s own inline CI-mirror step**, where it genuinely aborts the publish; and the guard's "exhaustive by construction" comment → three named, deliberate limits. Two guard defects fixed: it enumerated `mobile/` via `git ls-tree HEAD`, so a **local mirror run before committing was blind to a new directory** at exactly the point CLAUDE.md tells you to run it (now `git ls-files --cached --others --exclude-standard`; proven by probe), and its "clean" line now states what it does *not* inspect. Three **accepted over-triggers** are now pinned in the test table rather than left unexamined — icon/splash art (`mobile/assets/**` is in for the `require()`d Archivo fonts; the 4 PNGs beside them are referenced only from `app.config.js`, so an icon swap ships a byte-identical bundle and still publishes), test-only changes (36 `*.test.js` under `mobile/lib/`, 62 test/fixture files under `shared/` — real history: `206a0366` and `2941c7c8` each published on a test-only intersection), and the version bump itself. Narrowing `mobile/assets/**` to `fonts/**` was **rejected**: it would strand a future `require()`d image and, because the guard probes at top-level granularity, would make `assets` report UNCLASSIFIED. Relaxing `REQUIRED_PATTERNS` to permit `shared/**/*.test.js` exclusions was **rejected**: the only exclusion form GitHub offers is `!`, i.e. the denylist this PR exists to kill, and under-publishing a real shared change is the worse failure. 47 tests (was 41). |

| 533 | DEPAUDIT.3 — mobile audit green again: two `image-size` HIGHs accepted because NO patched release exists | The `npm audit (web runtime + mobile, high+)` job had been red on `main` since 2026-08-10 on GHSA-w3rx-r6r6-pgpr (ICNS infinite-loop DoS) + GHSA-5p2g-fcmc-qvqq (JXL/HEIF infinite-loop DoS), both against `image-size`, reached only via `expo@57 → @expo/metro@56 → metro@0.84.4` (declares `image-size: ^1.0.2`; lockfile resolves 1.2.1). Entry 479's lesson (`fixAvailable:false` usually means "blocked by a parent constraint — override it") was checked FIRST, against the registry rather than npm's report. Result: both advisories carry vulnerable range `<= 2.0.2` with `first_patched_version: None`, and **2.0.2 is the latest version ever published** (`npm view image-size versions`; upstream's last release 2025-04-02, subsequent commits README-only). There is no version to bump or override TO — even `metro@0.87.0` (latest) still declares `^1.0.2`. An override to 2.x would ALSO break metro: `metro/src/Assets.js` `getAssetData` calls image-size with a file-path string, and 2.x's sync API is Uint8Array-only. So this ships the **last-resort allowlist accept** in `mobile/.audit-allowlist.json` — its first non-empty state — with the code-path reason (metro's build-time asset-dimension probe over repo-owned images only; not in the shipped app bundle; worst case = a hung build from a malicious committed image) and `expires: 2026-11-15`. At expiry: re-run `npm view image-size versions`; if a patched release exists, fix via a metro-scoped override and delete both entries (the 479 playbook). No dep or lockfile change in this ship — verified `npm run check:dependency-audit:mobile` exits 0 with both accepts named. Rider: the `tests/dependency-audit.test.js` empty-state guard was narrowed, not deleted — web stays asserted-empty; mobile now asserts the accepted list is EXACTLY the two image-size ids (sorted exact-match), so any additional accept still fails `npm test` and forces a reviewed decision. |
