| 185 | SCHEDULE-PERSIST.1 — schedule calendar persists week/month/view in the URL (branch `schedule-week-persist`) | Operator-reported papercut: navigating to a future or past week and hitting browser refresh bounced the calendar back to "this week". **Root cause**: `ScheduleCalendar.jsx` initialised `weekStart` / `monthStart` / `viewType` from `new Date()` on every mount — there was no persistence layer, so a hard refresh lost the navigated position. **Fix**: URL params via `useRouter` / `usePathname` / `useSearchParams` from `next/navigation`. State now mounts from `?view=week\|month&week=YYYY-MM-DD&month=YYYY-MM-DD` (each param optional, falls back to today's Monday / month-start / `week`). A `useEffect` mirrors state → URL on every navigation via `router.replace` (no history entries — back-button skips out of the schedule entirely instead of having to undo N week clicks). **Why URL over localStorage**: (a) refresh-preserves works the same, (b) operators can bookmark "the week of the big event", (c) managers can paste "look at week-of-June-8 staffing" links to colleagues, (d) the back-forward browser buttons interact predictably. Net win vs the localStorage fallback. **Date-parsing gotcha**: `new Date('2026-05-20')` parses as UTC midnight, which under BST becomes 01:00 Sunday — wrong day. Added a `parseLocalDate(s)` helper that regex-validates the YYYY-MM-DD shape and uses the `(y, m-1, d)` ctor which is timezone-naive. Mirrors the inverse of `formatDate()`. Both `weekStart` and `monthStart` are snapped to their canonical boundary on parse (`getMonday`, `getMonthStart`) so a hand-pasted URL with mid-week date still lands on the right column. **Loop avoidance**: the URL-sync effect uses `window.location.search` (not the `searchParams` hook) to read existing params before merging, because including `searchParams` in the dep array would re-fire on every `router.replace` — `router.replace` updates the search params reference even when the URL is unchanged, creating a churn loop. `window.location.search` is safe inside `useEffect` (client-only). **Build/Suspense**: `useSearchParams` in a client component normally requires a `<Suspense>` boundary on the parent route — but `/schedule/page.js` already exports `dynamic = 'force-dynamic'`, which opts the route out of static optimization, so the Suspense requirement doesn't apply. Build passes clean with no Suspense warnings. **Files**: `src/components/ScheduleCalendar.jsx` only — `ScheduleTabs.jsx` doesn't need to know, `StudioOverviewStrip.jsx` already auto-refreshes off the calendar's range changes (OVERVIEW-REFRESH.1). Tests + lint + build remain green. |
| 184 | OVERVIEW-REFRESH.1 — Studio Overview auto-refreshes after schedule calendar mutations (branch `overview-auto-refresh`) | Operator-reported papercut: after assigning / unassigning / publishing / copying / bulk-assigning on the calendar, the Studio Overview strip above kept showing stale per-day coverage numbers and stale under-min flags until the page was hard-refreshed. **Root cause**: `StudioOverviewStrip.jsx` and `ScheduleCalendar.jsx` are siblings under `ScheduleTabs.jsx`. The strip's `useEffect` deps were `[range.from, range.to, locationId]` — those don't change on mutation, so the strip never refetched. The two siblings had no inter-component communication for "data changed under me". **Fix**: lift a `scheduleDataVersion` counter into `ScheduleTabs`. Wrap the bump in `useCallback` (`bumpDataVersion`) so its identity is stable across renders — otherwise `ScheduleCalendar`'s `fetchData` `useCallback` deps would churn every parent render and re-fire the mount-fetch loop. Pass `dataVersion={scheduleDataVersion}` to `StudioOverviewStrip` and add it to that component's `useEffect` deps so the strip refetches when it bumps. Pass `onDataChange={bumpDataVersion}` to `ScheduleCalendar`. **Calendar wiring**: introduce a `refreshAfterMutation` `useCallback` wrapping `await fetchData(); onDataChange?.()`. Replace the nine post-mutation `fetchData()` call sites — assign coach, partial-time-override save, ad-hoc block create, publish, copy-week, copy-month, bulk-assign, BlockDetailModal `onUnassign`, BlockDetailModal `onDeleteBlock` — with `refreshAfterMutation()`. Critically, leave `fetchData()` itself alone — the mount + navigation `useEffect(() => { fetchData() }, [fetchData])` does NOT bump the version, because the strip's existing `range`-dep already triggers its own refetch on navigation; bumping there too would cause a redundant overview fetch. The pattern: only fire `onDataChange` from intentional mutations, never from navigation refetches. **Files**: `src/components/ScheduleTabs.jsx`, `src/components/ScheduleCalendar.jsx`, `src/components/StudioOverviewStrip.jsx`. Tests + lint + build remain green. **Behavioural delta**: every coach assign / unassign / create / delete / publish / copy / bulk-assign now triggers a single overview refetch — under-min counts, coverage numbers, on-leave lines all update in real time without a page refresh. |

| 174 | SEG-TRIG.1 — segment_added / segment_removed sequence triggers | New trigger pair lets saved contact segments drive sequence enrolment alongside the existing status_change + tag_added triggers. Closes the long-standing Sequences backlog item. **Design**: contact_segments stores filter expressions only (no membership rows), so "added" / "removed" semantics required a durable snapshot. Mig 174 adds `contact_segment_memberships (segment_id, contact_id, added_at)` with PK on (segment_id, contact_id), reverse-lookup index on contact_id, RLS read-through-parent-segment, RESTRICTIVE deny on writes for authenticated + anon (service-role-only writes via the cron). **Cron**: new `/api/cron/sync-segment-memberships` (every 5 min, vercel.json updated, heartbeat seeded by mig 174). Finds every segment referenced by at least one active segment_* sequence trigger (operators' one-off /contacts page filters that never get wired into a trigger never get a snapshot — no wasted work), computes current membership via `applyAudienceFilterAsync`, diffs against stored, INSERTs additions and DELETEs removals, then fires triggers on the diff. Persist-before-fire ordering so a trigger handler crash can't re-fire the same diff on the next tick. **Trigger handlers**: `triggerSequencesForSegmentAdded(segmentId, contactIds)` + `triggerSequencesForSegmentRemoved(segmentId, contactIds)` in src/lib/sequences/triggers.js. `trigger_config.segment_id` is REQUIRED (a missing segment_id is treated as "no match" — a sequence without one would otherwise fire on every segment's diff). Audience-filter is still respected per-contact for cases where operators layer a narrower audience on top of segment membership. **Cascades**: contact deletion → membership row cascades, no segment_removed trigger fires (deletion is a different event class than churn-out-of-segment). Segment deletion → all membership rows cascade. Contact attribute change → next cron tick picks up the diff. **UI**: SequenceEditor extended with two new TRIGGER_TYPES entries + a segment-picker config panel that lazy-fetches `/api/contacts/segments?location_id=` the first time the operator picks a segment_* trigger. Empty-segments empty-state links to /contacts. **Tests**: 7 new cases in triggers.test.js (segment_added handler + segment_removed handler) + 7 in new segment-sync.test.js (no-active-triggers early exit, stable membership, additions-only, removals-only, churn-both-ways, segment_id dedup, malformed trigger_config). Sandbox can't run vitest (rolldown native binding still blocked) — runs on the Mac via `npm test`. |

| 172 | HOTFIX — supabase-js builder `.catch()` bug (728 stuck webhooks) | Pre-onboarding audit caught a silent failure mode: the supabase-js v2.45 builder objects (return value of `db.from(...)`, `db.rpc(...)`, `db.storage(...)`) are thenables, NOT real Promises. They have `.then` but no `.catch`. Pattern `await db.rpc('foo', {...}).catch(()=>{})` throws TypeError `e.rpc(...).catch is not a function` at runtime — the `.catch` is called on the builder object, not the resolved Promise. The TypeError gets caught by the outer try-block (if any) or surfaces in logs; the rpc itself never runs. Bleed in prod: 728 Postmark Open + Click events stuck in `postmark_webhook_queue` with `attempts=5/5` since May 13. Delivery / Bounce / SpamComplaint were unaffected (those code paths didn't use this pattern), so unsubscribe + bounce auto-unsub kept working. Fix: 7 sites across 3 files all converted to `try { await db.rpc(...) } catch {}` — `postmark-webhook-processor.js` (2 sites, the source of the stuck queue), `sequences/scheduler.js` (2), `sequences/steps.js` (3). Recovery: after deploy, `UPDATE postmark_webhook_queue SET attempts=0, error=NULL WHERE processed_at IS NULL AND attempts >= 5` resets the 728 rows; cron drains them in ~8 min; `SELECT recalculate_campaign_stats(id) FROM campaigns WHERE created_at > NOW() - INTERVAL '14 days'` brings open/click rollups current. Audit also verified zero other instances of the bug pattern in src/. |

Final tick (no more queued) flips to 'sent'. Throughput: 500/min/campaign × 3 campaigns = 1.5k sends/min site-wide; webhook firing spreads across the window instead of bursting, queue drain at 100/min stays well under Vercel's request rate. **(3) Schedule send:** UI date+time picker writes `scheduled_at` + `status='scheduled'`; the same cron's promote-step `UPDATE WHERE status='scheduled' AND scheduled_at<=now()` picks them up. **(4) Delete + cancel:** for draft/scheduled/queued statuses, direct Supabase delete (RLS already allows operator). For sending, UI sets `cancel_requested_at`; the send cron checks the flag between chunks, transitions status='cancelled' + flips remaining queued recipients to cancelled too. **(5) Live progress bar:** `CampaignEditor.jsx` adds a `useEffect` that polls the campaign row directly via Supabase every 3s while status is queued/sending, renders `Sending X / Y` next to a Cancel button, stops polling when status leaves the sending set. Status-aware button row replaces the old single "Send Campaign" button — draft shows Schedule + Send + Delete, scheduled shows Unschedule + Delete, queued/sending shows live progress + Cancel, sent/cancelled shows read-only summary. | 135 | CAMPAIGN.10 — fix audience-count returning 0 (postgrest-js select-overload trap) | The campaign editor's "0 contacts will receive this campaign" banner has been lying since CAMPAIGN.5 first shipped — every saved filter returned 0 regardless of how many contacts actually matched. CAMPAIGN.6/7/8/9 each chased a real-but-adjacent bug (embedded-resource filter losing its binding under count-only selects); CLASSIFY.1's denormalisation removed the embedded resource entirely, and only then was the underlying trap observable. **Root cause:** postgrest-js v2 has two `.select()` overloads. `PostgrestQueryBuilder.select(columns, options)` (the FIRST select after `.from()`) reads `options.head` + `options.count`, switches method to HEAD, and adds the `Prefer: count=exact` header. `PostgrestTransformBuilder.select(columns)` (any select chained AFTER a filter like `.eq` / `.not`) accepts ONLY columns; a second argument is silently ignored — JS doesn't enforce arity. `buildAudienceQueryAsync` did `.select('*')` first, set up the filters, then `computeCount` chained `.select('id', { count:'exact', head:true })` AFTER. The options vanished, the request stayed GET, no count Prefer was sent, supabase-js parsed `count` as `null`, and `count \|\| 0` rendered 0. **Fix:** `buildAudienceQuery` + `buildAudienceQueryAsync` now accept `{ columns, selectOpts }` so callers that want a count request it on the FIRST select. `computeCount` uses `{ columns: 'id', selectOpts: { count: 'exact', head: true } }`; everything else (`sendCampaign`, etc.) defaults to `('*', undefined)` and gets rows unchanged. **Diagnostic path:** the bug looked like a RLS / service-role-key issue because direct SQL as service_role returned 3,207 but the deployed API returned 0. Verified the key was correct via jwt.io (`role: "service_role"`), then via a one-off `/api/debug-supabase` endpoint that ran the exact prefilter with a single `.select('id', { count, head })` and returned 3,207 from the same `createServerClient()`. Diff between debug endpoint (works) and `computeCount` (broken) isolated the double-select pattern. Lesson: when supabase-js returns 0 from a count query but you expect rows, check whether you're chaining `.select()` twice — only the first call reads options. |

- Platform — location switch now updates the main view, not just the sidebar (operator: switching location changed the sidebar but the page stayed on the old location until a manual refresh). Root cause: LocationSwitcher sets the cookie + calls router.refresh(), which re-runs server components and refreshes the Sidebar's `user` prop, but client components inside a page fetch their data once on mount and don't re-run on a soft refresh. Fix: AppShell keys the page subtree (`<Fragment key={user.activeLocation.id}>`) so it remounts on a location switch — client components re-fetch for the new location. Key changes only on a location switch (not normal navigation); Fragment adds no DOM, zero layout impact. Estate-wide (every page).

- WA-COEX.6 — `account_update` webhook handling for the coexistence link lifecycle (gap found reading Meta's "Reconnect offboarded coexistence clients" doc while debugging a coexistence onboarding failure). When a coexistence client changes phone / reinstalls / re-registers the WhatsApp Business app, Meta AUTO-OFFBOARDS our Cloud API companion and fires `ACCOUNT_OFFBOARDED`; sends fail until an automatic re-link lands and `ACCOUNT_RECONNECTED` arrives (minutes). We subscribed `history`/`smb_app_state_sync`/`smb_message_echoes` but NOT `account_update`, so that outage would have been silent. New pure `parseAccountUpdateEvent` + `nextCoexistenceLinkState` reducer (whatsapp-coexistence.js) → state on `signup_meta.coex_link`, plus a manager push on each TRANSITION (not per webhook — Meta resends). Routed by **WABA id (`entry.id`)** because account_update carries no `metadata.phone_number_id`, scoped to `source='coexistence'` + `is_active` rows. LOAD-BEARING: `account_update` is a SHARED field (account review / violation / restriction / partner events ride it) — only the two coexistence events may touch link state, else a violation event reads as "phone reinstalled" (pinned in tests). First offboard wins on `offboarded_at` so resends don't reset the outage clock. `publicShape` exposes only `coex_link_status` + `coex_offboarded_at` (signup_meta carries the 2FA PIN). Update-error checked explicitly (supabase-js never throws — an unchecked error would read as "no numbers for this WABA"). DELIBERATE non-behaviour: does NOT auto-block sends — a state stuck `offboarded` would mute a location entirely, worse than the few sends that fail during a re-link; revisit after a live event pair. No migration (`signup_meta` from mig 405). Runbook §5.1 documents the new subscription + the reasoning.
- HOST-MASTER — host leads live on the Stillorgan MASTER profile, never AUTO-enrolled (mig 464 applied): Richard's 2026-07-31 call reversed the old "host leads are isolated at a hidden anchor location" model. `organizations.master_location_id` (Stillorgan for UN1T Group; NULL falls back to the host anchor, so no org is stranded) is where host signups + third-party-host event attendees are now placed AND matched — a signup from an existing member links to their real contact row instead of minting a doppelgänger. New contacts from those paths are stamped `contacts.automations_exempt=true`; matched existing contacts are NEVER flipped (a real member keeps behaving like a member). The flag is enforced at the single enrolment choke point (`enrolContacts`): every automatic source (triggers, crons, segments, dunning, inbound sequence webhook) drops exempt contacts and FAILS CLOSED if the flag read errors; `MANUAL_LIKE_SOURCE_TYPES = {manual, churn_radar}` bypasses it, because a staff member deliberately targeting a contact must include host leads. Broadcasts/campaigns/WhatsApp/Mia are unaffected — exempt ≠ unreachable. Confirmed host-event attendees now get `host:<slug>` + `event:<slug>` in BOTH tag systems (batched contact_tags delta pre-check so a re-confirmation doesn't re-query per attendee; a failed host load SKIPS tagging rather than writing a junk `host:host` tag). Contact profile: the existing Races card became "Events" with host attribution and is staff-visible (was Manager+, now the standard load-contact → assertLocationAccessOr404 idiom); a "No auto-enrol" chip + Manager+ toggle rides the header band (PUT gated by requireApiKeyOrManager, field stripped for API-key callers). **GOTCHA: the old `postmark.audience-scope` test is NO LONGER host-lead isolation** — it is plain multi-tenant location pinning; the auto-enrol protection is the enrolContacts gate. **Migration tool (`POST /api/admin/migrate-host-leads`, master/owner, dry-run unless `?dry=0`) is MOVE-ONLY by design**: it relocates unmatched anchor contacts to master (+ re-points their `contact_tags.location_id`, the only location-scoped read that matters) and never deletes or merges — an email collision with an existing master contact is reported in `needs_manual_merge` for a human to resolve via `/api/contacts/merge`, because a cross-location merge needs the full 48-FK child re-point that route already implements. Live state at build time: 1 anchor location holding 0 contacts, all 55 existing `host_contacts` already at Stillorgan, so the tool is a verified no-op today.
- AC-POWERSTATE.1 — LG ThinQ: an "already in that power state" rejection is no longer a fatal control error (live bug: the Womens bathroom AC failed 12 of 27 `bathroom_climate` fires 2026-07-28..31, `AC vendor refused the request: Command not supported in POWER_ON`; the Mens unit on the same events was 27/27 clean). LG rejects `operation: POWER_ON` when the unit is already running, and `setDeviceState` treated any `operation` failure as fatal — so the call threw before `airConJobMode`/`temperatureInUnits`/`airFlow` were sent (the bathroom never reached its configured 18°/high) AND the runner wrote no `ac_sessions` row, which meant **no auto-off was scheduled**, so the unit kept running and the next class's fire hit the same rejection. Self-perpetuating, which is why one unit was stuck in it and the other was not. Fix asks the device instead of pattern-matching LG's undocumented error wording: on an `operation` rejection we do one confirming `getDeviceState()` and, only if the unit is positively already in the requested power state, downgrade the error to a warning (`{ resource:'operation', already_in_state:true }`) and continue the resource sequence; an unreadable state, a state that disagrees, or an unrecognised operation mode all rethrow unchanged, so genuine power-on failures still surface to the operator. Symmetric for `POWER_OFF` (auto-off cron vs a unit already switched off at the wall). The confirming read doubles as the returned state when LG's control responses carry no echo. Zero cost on the happy path — the extra GET only happens on an already-failing call. Behaviour note: a unit found running outside the CRM is now adopted into a system session with a schedule-anchored auto-off rather than left to the `ac-external-rule` cron's flat `external_auto_off_minutes` cap. No migration; `class_climate` benefits identically (shared vendor layer).
- TICKET-UI-STATE.1 — the 2026-08-08 email audit's finding 4 family closed (confirmed HIGH + two mediums + a copy fix, all on the ticket inbox UI): (1) TicketReplyBox is now KEYED on the ticket id in TicketThread — its draft text, reply/note mode, added Cc/Bcc chips and attached files are local state, and without a key React kept the instance across a ticket switch, so member A's half-written reply (Bcc included) sat in member B's composer where Send delivered it to B's requester; the inbox already cleared the server-derived replyRecipients on switch, this extends the same rule to the operator-typed half (pinned in TicketThread.composer-reset.test.jsx, jsdom). (2) TICKET-FETCH-RACE.1: loadThread/loadQueue in TicketInbox applied responses unconditionally — a slow ticket-A read landing after ticket-B rendered A's thread under selectedId B (and handleSend posts to selectedId); same shape on the queue across a view/mailbox switch. Both now carry the AttachmentPreview requestFor-ref staleness guard (threadFor set in selectTicket/clearSelection, queueRequest per URL; stale responses skip state INCLUDING the spinner-clear, which belongs to the superseding request). Race pinned by resolving deferred fetches out of order in TicketInbox.race.test.jsx. (3) TICKET-COMPOSE-DISCARD.1: the compose modal closed on Esc/backdrop/X via the ui Modal defaults, silently discarding a fully-typed email — dismissing a DIRTY compose (any recipient, subject, text or file) now asks via bare confirm() (repo idiom), pristine still closes silently; deliberately NOT draft persistence, which the component header rules out (a fresh compose never inherits the last one's text — P3 backlog). (4) STATUS_META.closed.hint said a member reply "starts a new ticket" — fork-era copy predating Richard's 2026-08-07 reopen-not-fork call; now "reopens it", and the test asserts BOTH archived statuses say reopens and neither promises a new ticket. No migration, no route changes, web-only.
- EMAIL-REPLY-UNFILED.1 — a reply whose FILING fails after Postmark accepted it no longer answers with the raw DB error (audit 2026-08-08 finding 3: operator reads "insert failed" as "send failed", retries, member gets the email twice). The reply route now mirrors the compose route's posture and goes further: on msgErr-after-send it (1) records the delivered send as a `webhook_dead_letter` row — provider `email_ticket_reply` (deliberately NOT a REPLAYABLE_PROVIDERS key; replaying a send that happened would BE the double-send), location-stamped so integration health counts it, payload carrying recipients/signed body/postmark_message_id/threading anchor = everything needed to hand-file the missing message row; (2) still best-effort writes the `email_sends` row (delivery-webhook correlation + contact history both key on postmark_message_id) and advances the ticket to `pending` (the queue must stop saying "needs reply" about a member who has one — same reasoning as compose keeping its ticket row); (3) answers 500 with explicit "was sent… Do not resend" copy plus machine-readable `data: { sent: true, message_id }`. Client: `TicketInbox.handleSend` detects `data.sent`, refreshes thread+queue QUIETLY (a refresh hiccup repainting the banner would bury the do-not-resend sentence) and returns `{ ok:false, sent:true }`; `TicketReplyBox` keeps the draft — at that point it is the operator's only copy of what the member received. The send/patch/email_sends record construction was hoisted above the filing insert so both branches write the identical record. 5 new route tests incl. a `failWrites` harness helper (fails writes only — `state.errors` fails reads too, which would refuse before sending) and a pin that the NOTE branch keeps its plain 500 (nothing sent there, retry is safe). Residual, deliberately out of scope: the compose route's own two sent-but-unfiled branches remain untested and carry no `data.sent` flag.
- EMAILSTATUS-REMINT.1 — email_status='unsubscribed' can never come back (2026-08-08 audit finding 5, CONFIRMED HIGH): mig 492 retired the value (reputation-only column; consent is per-location in contact_location_preferences) but LOCCOMMS.5 missed the two writers in src/lib/marketing-consent.js — applyFormMarketingConsent and applyMarketingPreferencesBulk still mirrored opt-out to email_status='unsubscribed', and 7 live rows were re-minted within hours of the migration. With event-reminders + sequence steps hard-suppressing on the value, the cross-location over-blocking mig 492 removed was back. Fix: (1) both writers now touch email_status ONLY on opt-in (normalise NULL/'unsubscribed' residue → 'active'; bounced/complained never cleared; opt-out writes nothing — the consent rows above are the record); (2) mig 501 re-clears the re-minted rows AND adds CHECK (email_status IS DISTINCT FROM 'unsubscribed') so no future code path can reintroduce it — exclusion not allowlist, deliberately safe without live confirmation of the full value set; (3) the four readers still matching the retired value (event-reminders, sequences/steps, host-contact-list BLOCKED_EMAIL_STATUSES, person-aggregate NON_CONTACTABLE) drop it, mirroring booking-confirmations' earlier fix, + stale "the unsubscribe route stamps it" comments corrected; (4) tests pin opt-out-never-touches-email_status on both writers and non-suppression on the readers. ⚠️ mig 501 NOT applied (no DB access in the authoring session) — apply AFTER this deploys (reverse of the usual order: the CHECK depends on the code change), then run get_advisors BOTH types; the migration header documents this.
- EMAIL-COMPOSE-UNFILED.1 — the compose and forward routes' sent-but-unfiled branches brought up to the reply route's standard (the residual EMAIL-REPLY-UNFILED.1 left out of scope, plus forward, which had shipped in #1276 with the same gap). Both compose branches (ticket insert fails / message insert fails after Postmark accepted the send) and forward's msgErr branch had the right "Do not resend" copy but ZERO test coverage, no machine-readable flag, and no durable record of the delivered send — in compose's ticket-insert case NOTHING referenced the sent email anywhere. Now all three: (1) dead-letter the delivered send via deadLetterWebhook (providers `email_ticket_compose` / `email_ticket_forward` — deliberately not REPLAYABLE_PROVIDERS keys; location-stamped; payload = full re-fileable record — compose includes mailbox_id+contact_id, forward includes forwarded_message_id and the SENT quoted body a third party now has); (2) return `data: { sent: true, message_id }` (+ ticket_id on compose's msgErr, whose ticket row STAYS — now pinned by test); (3) compose best-effort writes the email_sends row in both failure branches (construction hoisted above the filing inserts, shared with the happy path — forward writes none by design, it doesn't go to the member). `failWrites` promoted from reply/route.test.js into the shared `_test-db.js` harness; 6 new tests across compose+forward. Client: TicketCompose detects `data.sent` → keeps modal+draft (already) and calls new optional `onSentUnfiled` prop; TicketInbox wires it to a quiet `loadQueue(true)` so a created-but-unfiled ticket appears behind the modal. TicketForward client needs nothing (no state changes on a forward by design; the copy in its error line suffices). Mobile has no compose/forward path.
- DEADLETTER-UI.1 + DEADLETTER-LOC.1 — the dead-letter queue gets its missing consumer (2026-08-08 audit P1: production-readiness gap 1). `webhook_dead_letter` had been accumulating GDPR-relevant rows nobody could see — unroutable/no-sender inbound mail, exhausted postmark_webhook_queue rows carrying bounces/complaints/RFC-8058 one-click unsubscribes, sent-but-unfiled ticket mail — because every email writer omitted `location_id` (so the per-location integration-health count never included them) and the master/owner JSON API had no UI. Three changes, surfacing only, zero auto-processing: (1) LOC.1 stamps `location_id` where knowable — inbound `no_sender`/`dedupe_release_failed` resolve recipient→mailbox→location via `bestEffortInboundLocation` (never throws; `no_matching_mailbox` stays NULL by design — inventing a location would repeat the oldest-active-location bug), and `postmark_queue` exhaustion + `postmark` ingest failures resolve MessageID→email_sends.location_id via new `resolveEmailSendLocation` (webhook-dead-letter.js); reply/compose/forward already stamped since #1279/#1280. (2) UI.1 — `/admin/webhook-dead-letter` (page + hub card, master/owner-gated like the API): tabs, provider filter, age/attempts/status, and per-row actions — Replay ONLY where the GET route's new `replayable` flag says the provider has an idempotent re-driver (email-family keys deliberately excluded — re-queueing resets the exhausted budget, replaying a sent email IS the double-send), plus new POST `[id]/resolve` (status `resolved`/`discarded`, both stamp `resolved_at`) as the human acknowledge path. Payload summaries are TEXT ONLY via new pure `src/lib/dead-letter-summary.js` — envelopes (addresses/subject/event), never TextBody/HtmlBody/text_body; html_body stays exclusive to the sanctioned sanitiser path. (3) integration-health's 'Webhook processing' row counts `location_id.eq.<loc> OR location_id.is.null` (orphans nag every studio rather than none), throws on count error so a query failure reads 'unknown' not green, detail says 'unresolved' (they're not all replayable), remedy links the new page. All three admin dead-letter routes registered in openapi.js. ~30 new tests (summary lib, resolve route, LOC stamping at all three writers, aggregator query shape).
- EMAIL-INBOUND-PUSH.1 + EMAIL-BADGE-M.1 — the 2026-08-08 audit's P1 product gap: inbound ticket mail now pushes staff, the way the WhatsApp and Instagram webhooks always have, and the mobile Email tab is badged. Push: new `src/lib/email-inbound-push.js` (pure gates + a swallow-own-errors db wrapper) called from the postmark-inbound webhook AFTER filing (main path + the crash-finish path, which owes the ping exactly when it owed the bump — the dead attempt's push ran after its bump, so a missing bump proves a missing push). Recipients are EXACTLY the people who could open the ticket — `email_inbox` resolved at the TICKET'S location through the full tier order (feature gate → per-user override → role template → code default) AND a grant on the TICKET'S mailbox (which on an append can differ from the delivering address), or elevated (master/owner-at-location; org admins deliberately not replicated, the mig 502 trade) — because a push carries sender + subject, so over-notifying IS the leak the grant model prevents. Hence fail-CLOSED on a failed links/grant lookup (templates/features degrade like resolvePushAllowedIds). Batching: one ping per ticket per unseen burst — gated on the PRE-increment unread_count (0 ⇒ ping; >0 ⇒ an outstanding ping nobody acted on), zeroed by the …/read route; no timers, no ledger, replay-safe via the route's own MessageID dedupe + the bump-state guard. Our own outbound arriving at our own webhook (compose sales@→accounts@, reply-all echo) files normally and pings NOBODY (own-address suppression from the already-fetched active mailbox list + POSTMARK_FROM_EMAIL). Category `email` registered everywhere the fails-closed invariant demands: MOBILE_PERMISSIONS `notify_email` (defaults MIRROR the email_inbox surface per role — master/manager/owner on; staff/reception/head_coach opt-in, pinned by test), NOTIFICATION_REGISTRY entry, and its OWN Android channel `email` (high, not messages-max: muting live chat must not mute the mailbox; channels are append-only so existing installs just gain it). Android delivery still blocked on Firebase (push audit 2026-07) — iOS/web-first by construction, nothing platform-aware here. Mobile: `email_inbound` routes to `/email/<ticket_id>` in notification-nav; the Email tab badge polls new `getTicketCount()` → `/api/email/tickets/count` (EMAIL-TICKET-CLEANUP.3's cheap route, same needs-reply predicate and two-level gate as the web sidebar badge) at the Messages badge's 60s/keep-last-count posture, only when the surface is reachable; the stale "there is no ticket count endpoint" comment in `(tabs)/_layout.jsx` deleted. All mobile changes pure JS — OTA-safe, no runtimeVersion bump. ~40 new tests (recipient/gate/payload unit suite, 6 webhook fan-out route tests incl. push-failure-cannot-fail-filing and the crash-finish pair, channel + defaults pins, nav + count-wrapper). No migration, no new routes.
- EMAIL-PUSH-ASSIGNEE.1 — the inbound-email push honours ownership, closing the loop EMAIL-INBOUND-PUSH.1 deliberately left open while `assigned_to` had no write path (EMAIL-ASSIGN.1-2 gave it one the same evening): a reply landing on an OWNED ticket now pings the owner alone (the WhatsApp webhook's assigned-conversation pattern), not everyone with mailbox access; an unowned ticket keeps the full eligible fan-out. The rule that matters: the assignee is preferred ONLY when they still pass the exact same gates as everyone else (`email_inbox` at the ticket's location + grant on the ticket's mailbox, or elevated) — a claim is not a licence to keep receiving subject lines after the grant/permission/membership behind it is revoked. An assignee the gates refuse is treated as NO assignee: the stale owner gets nothing (the leak) AND the mail still announces to whoever can open it, rather than sitting unseen behind a claim its holder cannot read. Implementation is one narrowing step in `maybeNotifyInboundEmail` (`ids.includes(assignedTo) ? [assignedTo] : ids` after the existing recipient resolution — notify_email opt-out and the master switch still apply inside sendPush, location-scoped) plus `assigned_to` on the webhook's two ticket selects (threaded append + finishDedupedDelivery; the create path passes null — no auto-assign). Batching/own-address/pre-unread gates unchanged. TDD: 3 lib tests (owner-only; grant-revoked fallback; left-the-location fallback) + the route fan-out describe extended to pin `assignedTo` on all three paths. No migration, no new routes, no mobile change.
- WA-TPL-BTN — a template submit failed live with Meta code 100 / subcode 2388060 and the operator saw only "Invalid parameter". Two defects: (1) `createTemplate`/`editTemplate` threw `result.error.message`, and on the `message_templates` endpoints that field is the same generic string for a dozen unrelated causes — the actionable sentence ("Buttons can't have any variables, newlines, emojis or formatting characters.") lives in `error_user_title`/`error_user_msg`/`error_data.details` and was discarded on the way to the UI; a failed submit inserts no row, so nothing was recoverable afterwards either. (2) Nothing checked the buttons before the round trip. New `formatMetaError()` (`src/lib/whatsapp-meta-error.js`) leads with Meta's user-facing copy and keeps code/subcode for lookup; new `templateButtonsError()`/`componentsButtonsError()` (`src/lib/whatsapp-template-buttons.js`) enforce the button rules — plain-text labels only (no variables, line breaks, emoji, or WhatsApp formatting delimiters), 25 chars, per-type required fields, Meta's counts (10 total / 2 URL / 1 phone) — in the editor (live hint under the Buttons card + submit gate) and server-side on both POST /api/whatsapp/templates and the resubmit route, so a direct API caller hits the same wall. A URL variable is allowed exactly where Meta allows it (one variable, at the very end of the link, with an example value), so a dynamic-URL template synced back from Meta still resubmits — the builder can't author that example yet and the message says so. Emoji detection uses `\p{Extended_Pictographic}`, which deliberately does not match `*` or digits (Emoji-property but legal button characters). 25 tests including the verbatim live error object.
- NOENGSUP.1 — engagement-based email suppression RETIRED entirely (operator decision, Richard 2026-08-12: "I don't want any suppression of users from marketing, just because they don't engage today doesn't mean they won't engage in 6 months when they want to train"). EMAIL-HYGIENE.1 had imported a general email-marketing rule — suppress anyone who hasn't opened in 90 days — into a gym, where a member going quiet for a season and returning in January is the normal customer shape, not a dead address. It was suppressing the win-back campaign from exactly the people it was written for: of the 1,107 contacts the 12 Aug 05:15 run stamped, 913 were `dormant`. (That run was itself a one-off cliff: the sweep's "first marketing send >90 days ago" guard, meant to protect new contacts, fires for a whole cohort at once on a list whose first send ever was 13 May — see HYGREL.1.) Removed: the `email-engagement-sweep` cron route, `src/lib/email-hygiene.js`, the vercel.json entry, and (mig 537) its `cron_heartbeats` row — a cron with a heartbeat row that never runs alerts as stale forever. mig 537 also clears every engagement-origin stamp: 912 released, derived by predicate (`no OPEN suppress escalation`), leaving 21. KEPT DELIBERATELY: hard-bounce and spam-complaint suppression, and the repeat-bounce sweep. Not opening is a preference; not existing is a fact, and continuing to hit dead mailboxes is what gets a sending domain throttled — which would cost delivery to the people who do open. Consequence that had to ship with it: `contacts.email_suppressed_at` used to mean two things and now means one (repeat bounces, always with an `email_bounce_escalations` row behind it), so the preference centre STOPS clearing it on re-consent — a customer click would otherwise un-suppress a bouncing address AND silently auto-close its escalation, since `bounce-escalation-sweep` reads a cleared stamp as `stamp_cleared_externally`. Same rule as EMAILREP.4 for the same reason: consent is not evidence the mailbox works. Also corrected everywhere the old meaning was asserted: the audience-count label ("inactive 90+ days" → "suppressed for repeat bounces"), the sequence-step skip reason, buildAudienceQuery's comment, the list-health release's OpenAPI description, the reconciliation release_note, and the EMAIL_DELIVERABILITY checklist. Verified live after applying: 912 released, 21 suppressed (all open bounce escalations), heartbeat row gone, mailable marketing audience 2,482 → 3,398.

- IMPACTCAT.1 — the contact delete-impact preview is derived from the FK catalog, not a hand-maintained list (mig 538, **NOT APPLIED** — the code falls back until it is). `getContactImpact` counted dependent rows from three constants in `src/lib/contact-merge.js` totalling **21** (table, column) pairs. `pg_constraint` says **80** columns reference `contacts(id)`: 51 CASCADE, 27 SET NULL, 1 RESTRICT, 1 NO ACTION. So the dialog under-reported the cost of a delete by ~60 columns — InBody scans, heart-rate sessions, consultations, coaching goals, achievements, health metrics, monthly targets, Strava activities, devices, app claim tokens, and `contact_location_preferences` (per-location marketing consent) — and the operator clicked the button believing the smaller number. Same drift migration 533 fixed for the MERGE path, fixed the same way: `public.contact_delete_impact(uuid)` reads `pg_constraint` at call time and counts per (table, column) with `format('%I')` dynamic SQL, **in one round trip** rather than 80 (every referencing column on a >1k-row table has a leading index). Where 533 RAISES on composite / self-referencing FKs — a merge cannot re-point them safely — this one counts them: it is a read-only preview, so refusing to answer helps nobody; composite keys are narrowed to their `contacts.id` member by pairing `conkey` with `confkey`, and partitions are excluded so a cloned FK cannot double-count. **The two blockers are the point.** `person_groups.primary_contact_id` (RESTRICT, NOT NULL) and `offer_purchases.contact_id` (**NO ACTION**) both raise an FK violation on delete — they differ only in deferrability — and neither was ever reported; `block_delete` existed in the return shape with nothing populating it. `ContactEditDeleteActions.jsx` hides the type-to-confirm input entirely while `block_delete` is non-empty, so filling it is what stops an operator attempting a delete that can only end in a raw Postgres error. Labels: the hand-written ones from the three constants become an OVERRIDE map keyed `table.column`, everything else gets a mechanical humanised table name (`member_health_metrics` → "member health metrics"), suffixed with the column when it isn't the plain `contact_id` so two references from one table don't render as identical lines. The three WhatsApp tables are CASCADE/SET NULL in the catalog but keep landing in `redact_on_delete` via an explicit override applied AFTER bucketing — mig 094's PII scrub, not the FK rule, is what makes those kept rows GDPR-safe. **Deployment shape:** mig 538 is applied by hand and Vercel auto-deploys `main`, so hard-depending on the function would have broken the delete dialog in prod; the three constants are KEPT as the fallback (and as the label source, and as `redactWhatsAppForContact`'s work list) and the RPC being absent falls through to exactly today's behaviour. That fallback is **observable, not silent**: a new `partial: true` on the returned object — set when the RPC is unavailable or any individual count errored — surfaces in both consumers as one amber line saying the list may be incomplete. `countAt` still swallows its errors (best-effort preview, deliberate), but a preview whose whole job is to say how much gets destroyed must never report a confident 0 when it did not manage to look — the same class of defect as the under-reporting. Output shape and field names unchanged (`{ table, column, label, count }`, keyed `` `${t.table}.${t.column}` ``). 21 new tests.
- MERGEPREV.1 — the merge dialog's "After merge" preview promised an outcome the merge does not produce, and hid five it does. `ContactMergeModal` kept a local `previewMergedFields()` commented "Mirrors src/lib/contact-merge.js#pickMergedFields"; it had drifted BOTH ways, and nothing compared the two copies so neither drift was visible. (1) It previewed `pipeline_stage_slug` as a merged field. That column is denormalised and owned entirely by `sync_contacts_pipeline_stage_slug_trigger` (mig 155), which recomputes it as the stage of the contact's MOST RECENTLY CREATED OPEN DEAL — and a merge re-points the loser's deals onto the survivor, so the trigger then re-runs across the combined set and the newest open deal is frequently the loser's. The preview claimed "survivor wins unless empty", i.e. often the exact opposite of the result. Verified live: 0 of 8,580 contacts carry a slug that disagrees with the trigger, so the column is fully derived and a browser-side prediction can only ever be right by coincidence. The row is gone; in its place a note says the stage is recalculated from the combined deals after the merge. The per-contact "Stage:" line in the survivor PICKER is untouched — that one is factual (each contact's own current stage) and is what the operator picks on. (2) The local copy also omitted `first_name`, `last_name`, `trial_credits_remaining`, `lead_created_at` and `last_emailed_at`, all of which the merge writes — so the operator confirmed changes never shown. The modal now imports the real `pickMergedFields` (safe from a client component: `contact-merge.js` pulls in only `./log`, which is console-only, and the function is pure) and RENDERS THE ROWS FROM ITS OUTPUT, so a field added to the merge appears on its own rather than needing a second edit. Empty-on-both fields are skipped. Known display gap, deliberately not closed: the modal is fed `CONTACT_LIST_FIELDS` (narrowed by PERF.2), which carries 5 of the 11 merged columns, so the others cannot render — a display gap only, since the client posts two ids and `mergeContacts` re-reads both rows with `select('*')` server-side, and the note now states the fill rule covers fields not listed. First test file for this modal: 4 cases, the load-bearing one importing `pickMergedFields` and asserting the rendered rows match its output exactly (re-introducing the stage row fails it).
- AGENT-REQ-UX.1 — the /approvals Agent requests tab decides INLINE (operator ask, Richard 2026-08-24: "this should be actionable under the agent request tab … not have to go onto the next page"). Previously the tab was a generic click-through list to /settings/customer-agent/requests; every other consumer of the queue (settings page, inbox thread card, mobile Customers tab) already decided in place through PATCH /api/agent/membership-requests/[id]. New `AgentRequestDecideCard` uses that same route (atomic pending-claim, Glofox execution on approve, in-thread confirmation / decline notice all server-side), renders the Saved-the-member option on retention-flagged cancellations, surfaces execution failures ("Approved, but the Glofox action failed (<code>) … the customer has NOT been confirmed"), and answers a 409 with "Already decided elsewhere — refresh". Badge counts drop immediately on decide; the card keeps its outcome until the next refresh. Two information gaps closed on BOTH review surfaces (/approvals card + settings page): (1) machine flag codes were rendered verbatim (`Reason: "prior_attendance"`) — new `src/lib/approvals/agent-request-why.js` translates every routeToReview / MIA-BOOK code (prior_attendance, needs_credit_grant, account_*, attendance_check_failed, booking_failed:<CODE> incl. plain-English no-credits, booking_rejected, superseded_duplicate, draft-mode default) into a what-happened + what-to-do line, while pause/cancellation reasons — the CUSTOMER's own words — render as a quote and are never confused with codes (`customerWords` prefers customer_note, falls back to details.reason for non-booking kinds only); (2) no contact detail for the Glofox lookup — the provider and the full-history GET now carry contacts.email/phone, shown as click-to-copy chips ("Glofox lookup") on both surfaces. Provider items gain contactId/contactEmail/contactPhone/retentionFlagged (mobile shape untouched). Web-only — no migration, no new routes, no shared/ or mobile/ changes (no OTA), no new permission keys (the tab-visibility key and the PATCH decide key are both approvals_agent_requests, so anyone who can see the tab can act). ~15 new tests (why-translator table, provider field mapping).
- AGENT-RETRY.1 — a failed agent-request execution is a fix-then-retry, not a dead end (operator ask, Richard 2026-08-24: approved Kate Byrne's booking, Glofox rejected on YOU_HAVE_NO_CREDITS_LEFT, and the row "died" — the route 409'd every re-decision, so after granting the credit the booking had to be recovered by hand-editing the row). The PATCH route now accepts a re-APPROVE on a failed EXECUTING-kind row (isRetryableFailure): fresh atomic claim on status='failed' (two concurrent retries race the predicate, loser 409s — the double-execution guarantee is unchanged), execution re-runs, confirmation sends on success. Approve-only: decline on a failed row still 409s (the customer was never confirmed; a days-late decline notice is noise), and non-executing kinds (pause/cancellation) stay shut. THE BUTTON ONLY RETRIES, NEVER FIXES — the operator sorts the account in Glofox first (the one automated fix stays: needs_credit_grant rows grant the trial credit inside approval, as before). Surfaces: (1) the /approvals inline card's failed outcome now shows what went wrong (new failureExplanation — no-credits and NOT_EXECUTABLE get plain-English fix instructions, unknown codes stay visible) plus a "Fixed it — retry" button in place (first decision decrements the badge once; a retry doesn't double-count); (2) /settings/customer-agent/requests gets a "Failed — fix & retry" section above the pending queue — populated by retryOffered, the deliberately STRICTER UI gate: rows with a parseable details.starts_at are offered only while the class is still in the future, ones without fall back to a 48h decided-at window, so the section can't accumulate stale history (the ROUTE stays permissive — a deliberate operator retry on an edge case isn't refused). Retry-mode cards show the failure line and only the retry button. Web-only, no migration, no new routes, no mobile/shared change. 15 new tests (recovery helpers, route claim-predicate/409s/second-failure, failure copy). Parked, still open: failed executions don't badge or count anywhere until someone visits — the "should failed executions alert staff" call from INBOX-APPROVALS remains unanswered.
- AGENT-RETRY.2 — failed agent-request executions ride the approvals badge (Richard 2026-08-24: "lets add failures to the badge count" — until now a failed execution counted NOWHERE and was only seen if someone happened to open the requests page). The agent_requests provider now runs a second bounded query (status='failed', executing kinds, decided within 30 days) filtered through retryOffered — the same class-still-in-future / 48h-recency gate as the settings section — and ships the survivors as a NEW `failedItems` array on the provider payload, with `count` (tab badge, sidebar badge via countPending, mobile tile) including them. failedItems is deliberately SEPARATE from `items` (older mobile bundles render items verbatim; keeping failed rows out means a not-yet-updated phone shows a slightly higher badge than its list rather than a card whose Decline can only 409). Registry passes failedItems through (defaults [] for every other provider — none of the others have the concept). Web /approvals tab renders failed cards FIRST under a "Failed — fix & retry" heading (that customer has been waiting longest and was told nothing): red Failed chip, what-went-wrong line (failureExplanation), and "Fixed it — retry" as the only decision (decline would 409); a successful retry decrements the badge once via the existing countedDecided guard. countPending fetches the failed window without the contact embed and counts in JS (retryOffered reads details/decided_at per row, so a head-count can't answer). MOBILE (Richard: "yes add the mobile retry cards too" — this half PUBLISHES AN OTA at 100% on merge, mobile/lib + components + app are bundle paths): the Customers tab renders the same failed-first section — failedQueue helper (urgency-sorted like customerQueue: a failed booking for a class starting soon tops the hub), CustomerApprovalCard grows a fix-&-retry mode (red Failed chip, provider-precomputed `failedWhy` line so mobile needs no explainer lib, retry as the only button — onApproveCustomer's existing executed.ok===false Alert already surfaces a repeat failure honestly). No migration, no new routes, no shared/ change, no new permission keys. 7 new tests (4 provider: segregation, gate, count agreement incl. the head-count + JS-count sum; 3 mobile failedQueue).
- AGENT-FUNNEL-CREDITS.1 — prior attendance no longer blocks a funded booking, and approval cards show the account balance (Richard 2026-08-25, prompted by Vanessa Schmid's case: flagged prior_attendance despite a trial membership with 3 credits — "if we have granted her credits and is looking to book lets use the available balance on the account"). PIPELINE (class-booking-processor): the cheap last_attended_at pre-gate no longer short-circuits to review; identity resolves first, attendance is judged (local stamp, else the wide 5-year Glofox check — uncertain read still fails safe), and an attended returner then hits a BALANCE gate: credits > 0 → book against them; credits null/0 but CRM-synced glofox_membership_status='active' → book (computeCreditsRemaining is null for BOTH "no credits" and "membership without per-class credit records", so the synced status breaks the tie; Glofox arbitrates and a rejection routes to review as booking_failed → the fix-&-retry flow); otherwise → review as prior_attendance, which NOW MEANS "attended before AND nothing to book with". Rule 5's real invariant is untouched: a returner is never auto-granted a fresh trial (findOrCreateGlofoxMember is not even called on the attended path — pinned by test), and the never-attended paths (create+trial, needs_credit_grant) are unchanged. whyFlagged copy for prior_attendance rewritten to the new semantics (grant a credit or set up a membership, then approve). CARDS: new `accountSummaryLine` (agent-request-why.js) renders the membership fields the Glofox sync already denormalises onto contacts — "The UN1T Trial (trial, not started) · 3 credits left" / "No membership on file · 0 credits left" — no live API call, last-sync freshness. Provider embeds the four fields (both pending + failed queues) and precomputes `accountLine` AND `why` per item (the failedWhy pattern), so mobile needs no lib; rendered on the web decide card, the settings RequestCard (GET route embed widened), and mobile's CustomerApprovalCard — which also gains the why-flagged line on pending cards (a gap from AGENT-RETRY.2: mobile only explained FAILED cards). This is the staff-side half of the mia-audit "credits blindness" finding; Mia's customer-side can_book pre-check (plan D) is still open. ⚠️ Merge publishes an OTA (mobile bundle paths). 12 new tests (6 processor balance-gate incl. no-trial-grant pin, 5 accountSummaryLine, 1 provider enrichment).
